candidates.title: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)
candidates.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. Built on Mathlib with only Lean's standard axioms.

candidates.title: Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem and the Rothschild–Stein theory
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the regularity theory of Hörmander operators: second-order operators built from smooth vector fields X_1, ..., X_q (and possibly a drift X_0) whose iterated commutators span the tangent space at every point. It proves Hörmander's 1967 theorem that such operators are hypoelliptic: every locally integrable weak solution of X_0 u + sum X_i^2 u + c u = g with smooth data is smooth. It then develops the Rothschild–Stein theory (Acta Math. 1976), following Bramanti and Brandolini's "Hörmander Operators" (2023): lifting and approximation of the fields by the generators of a homogeneous group; the homogeneous fundamental solution and singular-integral estimates on homogeneous groups; and the sharp interior estimates, by which a distributional solution of sum X_i^2 T = f with f in W^{k,p}_X or C^{k,alpha}_X is a function in W^{k+2,p}_X or C^{k+2,alpha}_X, for every k >= 0, and at k = 0 with a drift. The formalization also proves the formal Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff theorem, Chow–Rashevskii connectivity, and the Nagel–Stein–Wainger theorems on control balls (ball-box, volume and doubling, comparison of distances), uniformly over compact sets.

candidates.title: What Does the Refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis Mean for Learning Theory?
candidates.abstract:
Two recent works by OpenAI and Anthropic refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). They count the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF on $n$ variables in time $2^{n/(\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}}$. Many fine-grained lower bounds in learning theory rest on ETH and its relatives. We determine what the refutation changes for learning.

The answer is a locality principle: the new algorithms speed up learning when each labeled example constrains few bits of the hypothesis, and under the CNF form of the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis, which survives, the speed-up ends at $\Theta(\log N)$ bits. Three transitions make the principle precise.

Locality. Call a class with $N$-bit descriptions $\kappa$-local if each label depends on at most $\kappa$ description bits, as for quantized models on sparse data. Then proper PAC learning, exact version-space counting and sampling, and the halving algorithm run in time $\mathrm{poly}(m)\cdot 2^{o(N)}$ on samples of size $m$ for $\kappa=o((\log N)^{1/4}/\sqrt{\log\log N})$, and proper PAC learning at constant accuracy does so for $\kappa=o(\sqrt{\log N})$. At inverse-polynomial accuracy, proper learning of $\kappa$-local classes is equivalent to $\kappa$-SAT, up to a factor $2$ in the locality. Under CNF-SETH, consistency for binarized perceptrons on $O(\log N)$-sparse data needs time $2^{(1-\gamma)N}$ for every $\gamma>0$.

Accuracy. Exact empirical risk minimization, proper agnostic learning and the exponential mechanism reduce to tensor contractions over a truncated polynomial ring. As a consequence, the Sparse Max-SAT Hypotheses of Alman and Vassilevska Williams are false. At constant accuracy, proper learning is SAT parameterized by formula length. With quasi-linear PCPs this gives a $2^{N/\mathrm{polylog}\,N}$ lower bound under a length form of ETH, which replaces Gap-ETH for reductions of quasi-linear size. At accuracy $N^{-3}/8$, the Max-3-SAT Hypothesis forces time $2^{(1-o(1))N}$.

Treewidth. Exact inference in graphical models of bounded degree and arity takes time $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. On expanders this beats every elimination order and every structured DNNF. Under $\#$CNF-SETH, time $2^{(1-\gamma)\mathrm{tw}}$ is again necessary once a model may have $\mathrm{tw}^{O(1)}$ variables.

We also take stock of the conditional lower bounds of learning theory: which ones fall, and which ones survive on which hypothesis. The bound for training one ReLU loses its proof, because its hypothesis about Densest $k$-Subgraph on bounded-degree graphs is false. The next obstacle is a permutation problem. On difference vectors $e_i-e_j$, empirical risk minimization for real-valued halfspaces is weighted Feedback Arc Set, which the new algorithms do not reach.

candidates.title: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:

The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

candidates.title: Explicit uniformly bounded bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every dimension
candidates.abstract: We construct uniformly bounded orthonormal bases for homogeneous holomorphic polynomials on complex unit spheres. Fix d >= 2 and N >= 0, and put m = d-1 and L = N+d-1. For each multi-index alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_d) of nonnegative integers with sum N, define s_b(alpha) = b + alpha_1 + ... + alpha_b, 1 <= b <= m, and the normalized monomial M_alpha(z) = sqrt((N+d-1)! / ((d-1)! alpha_1! ... alpha_d!)) z_1^alpha_1 ... z_d^alpha_d. Let F be the normalized Fourier matrix, with entries F_(t,s) = L^(-1/2) exp(2 pi i t s/L), for 1 <= t,s <= L. For each increasing m-element subset T = {t_1,...,t_m} of {1,...,L}, define P_T(z) = sum_(|alpha|=N) det[F_(t_a,s_b(alpha))] exp(2 pi i sqrt(2) sum_r alpha_r^2) M_alpha(z), where the determinant is over 1 <= a,b <= m. These polynomials form an orthonormal basis with respect to surface measure of total mass one on the complex unit sphere. Their absolute values on the closed unit ball are bounded by a constant depending only on d, independently of N and T. The construction and proof are formalized in Lean.

candidates.title: Yu-Wang-Samworth 2015: population-gap eigenspace and singular-subspace perturbation bounds
candidates.abstract:
A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the principal population-gap perturbation results of Yi Yu, Tengyao Wang and Richard J. Samworth, "A useful variant of the Davis-Kahan theorem for statisticians" (Biometrika 102 (2015) 315-323). This single Palomar entry compares both conclusions of Theorem 2 and both displays of Corollary 1 for eigenspaces of real symmetric matrices, together with the right- and left-singular-subspace conclusions of Theorem 3 for general real matrices and two supporting equivalences between its Gram-eigenvector formulation and the paper's paired singular-vector equations.
The common idea is that every separation hypothesis in Theorems 2 and 3 is stated entirely in terms of the population object. Theorem 2 uses the population eigenvalue gap min(lambda_(r-1)-lambda_r, lambda_s-lambda_(s+1)); Theorem 3 applies the same idea to the squared singular spectrum, with the additional factor (2 sigma_1 + ||A-hat-A||_op). No sample eigenvalue or singular-value gap is assumed, so the sample frame is arbitrary among admissible orthonormal frames at the selected block, including under multiplicity.
The selected results have deliberately different source dispositions. Theorem 2 is source-exact. Corollary 1 writes out the unit normalization inherited from its introduction as the d=1 case of Theorem 2; the standalone printed display omits that normalization and its second conclusion is false without it. Theorem 3 is source-corrected: its printed convention sigma^2_(rank(A)+1) := -infinity makes the denominator infinite at a rank boundary and yields a false assertion. The compared statement instead uses the ambient Gram-spectrum convention used by the paper's own proof, with singular values zero past rank, while retaining the printed restriction 1 <= r <= s <= rank(A). Because this one entry contains that correction, its source relationship is conservatively recorded as `adapts`.

A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.

On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). candidates.title: Log-square quadrupolar correlation decay in two-dimensional RP2 and RP3 models
candidates.abstract: For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor RP2 and RP3 director models, the absolute quadrupolar two-point correlation is bounded by C exp(-c (log(2+r))^2) at every finite bound on the dimensionless coupling. The positive constants are uniform over finite square-lattice subgraphs, arbitrary signed edge couplings within that bound, and observation sites; r is the integer lattice infinity distance. The compared statements use explicit normalized spherical product measures and Gibbs-integral quotients, with observable (n_x dot n_y)^2 - 1/3 or - 1/4, respectively. No response estimate or decay certificate is assumed. This registry interface selects the two finite-volume bounds. It does not assert exponential decay at all temperatures or the absence of every thermodynamic or topological transition. The larger development also contains local-limit and high-temperature results, which are not selected by this Comparator entry.

candidates.title: Continuity of the phase transition for planar random-cluster and Potts models with 1 <= q <= 4 (Theorems 1, 2 and 3)
candidates.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius and Tassion (arXiv:1505.04159v1). Theorem 3: for the random-cluster model on the square lattice with any real cluster weight q >= 1, at its critical point p_c, the following are equivalent: the origin lies in an infinite cluster with probability 0 under the wired measure; equality of the free and wired measures; infinite susceptibility of the free measure; sub-exponential decay of the free one-arm probability; and the RSW bound for free boundary conditions at distance n. Theorem 2: for 1 <= q <= 4 the wired measure at p_c gives probability 0 to the origin lying in an infinite cluster. Theorem 1: for the q-state Potts model with q = 2, 3, 4, the monochromatic Gibbs measure at beta_c gives its own colour at the origin probability exactly 1/q, so the phase transition is continuous. The critical points are the genuine phase-transition thresholds, whose existence the theorems assert; four further theorems prove that these critical points and the infinite-volume measures are unique; beyond this statement surface, the development also proves p_c = sqrt(q)/(1 + sqrt q) for every q >= 1 (PottsContinuity.BD12.isRCCriticalPoint_sqrt) and beta_c = log(1 + sqrt q) for every integer q >= 2 (PottsContinuity.Thm1.isPottsCriticalPoint_log_sqrt); these identifications are not checked by Comparator. The infinite-volume measures are limits along every exhaustion of the lattice, and their existence and uniqueness are proved. The external results that the paper cites and the proof uses (the value of p_c and the crossing estimates of Beffara-Duminil-Copin, the contour identity of the parafermionic observable in the form used in Section 4 of the paper, Theorem 4 of the paper, the Edwards-Sokal coupling, FKG and comparison inequalities, the domain Markov property, planar duality and topology) are proved here or taken from Mathlib; the Jordan-Schoenflies theorem and Brouwer's fixed-point theorem come from vendored libraries, and circle-degree and Jordan-curve facts from the Tau Ceti library. The only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

candidates.title: Erdős problem #257: all base irrationality of the reciprocal Mersenne subseries for every infinite reciprocal summable support, with weighted mass and positive cover extensions, achievement set geometry, and exact greedy membership criteria
candidates.abstract:
Erdős problem 257 asks whether the sum over a in A of 1/(2^a - 1) is irrational for every infinite set A of positive integers. The principal theorem compared here settles the whole reciprocal summable regime at every integer base: if A is infinite and the sum over a in A of 1/a converges, then the sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1) is irrational for every integer b at least 2 (ReciprocalSupport.irrational_supportPowerSeries_of_summable_reciprocal). No pairwise coprimality, periodicity, density, or powerful support hypothesis appears. Paul Erdős printed the pairwise coprime case of exactly this statement, at every integer base, in 1968, and stated there that pairwise coprimality can be removed by a longer argument he did not print. The theorem compared here is that stated extension, proved independently. No priority over Erdős is claimed and no identification with his omitted argument is asserted. The consequence for the parent problem is a boundary condition: any infinite support witnessing a counterexample has divergent reciprocal sum. Erdős problem 257 remains open.
The readers are number theorists working on irrationality for Lambert type and reciprocal Mersenne series, and analysts who study subsum sets of convergent series. Erdős (1948) proved irrationality of the full support value at every integer base; Erdős (1968) proved the pairwise coprime reciprocal summable case; Duverney and Tachiya (2019) treated the squarefree support at every base 2^j; Tao and Teravainen proved the prime support case at base two. Duverney and Tachiya record the Erdős and Graham conjecture that the sum is irrational for every increasing sequence of exponents and describe their corollary as support for it. Each covers one distinguished family; none covers an arbitrary reciprocal summable support, nor the reciprocal divergent supports below.
Three theorems state sufficient criteria that do not ask for reciprocal summability. Write h(a) for the P part of a at a finite nonempty prime set P. DivisibilityWeightedSupport.divisibilityWeightedClaim has two clauses: convergence of the sum over a in A of h(a)/(a(b^h(a) - 1)) at a fixed base b at least 2, for infinite A avoiding 0, gives irrationality at that base; the same weighted mass at base two on a host H avoiding 0 gives irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of H. VariableExponentCover.strengthenedPositiveCoverClaim gives that hereditary all base conclusion for every infinite subset of the host of a positive fractional divisor cover of convergent one inverse power cost, and MixedWeightedCover.mixedSupportClaim combines the two criteria on one observation scale. LiteralWeightedCover.exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host makes the weighted enlargement strict: a weighted host of divergent reciprocal mass admitting no strengthened cover, whose infinite subsets are irrational at every integer base at least 2. DyadicObservationSummability records dyadic averaging estimates for weighted observation masses.
FinitePeriodNoncollapse is exact finite support arithmetic: for finite nonempty F of positive exponents and integer base b at least 2, the reduced denominator of the sum over n in F of 1/(b^n - 1) is coprime to b, the order of b modulo it is exactly lcm F, and lcm F is strictly below that denominator once it is at least 2. RationalTailRigidity adds four necessary conditions on a hypothetical rational value p/(2^c v): an unbounded positive integer tail orbit with exact doubling recurrence, a sublogarithmic bound on zero windows of the divisor incidence coefficients, a reciprocal mass floor from the order of 2 modulo an odd reduced denominator when the reciprocals are summable, and a dyadic mass alternative. None contradicts a rational value. BooleanMobiusCarry gives exact coordinates: for an integer p and a positive natural q, a support avoiding 0 with some positive element and base two value p/q exists precisely when a positive square root bounded integer carry has Boolean Moebius normalised quotient. That characterisation permits finite supports, so it excludes no rational value.
AchievementSetGeometry and FairCoding describe the set of all subsums of that series at base two. For every set J of allowed digit positions the supported coding map is injective with compact nowhere dense range, the range is perfect when J is infinite, and the Lebesgue measure obeys an exact dichotomy: 2^(-|F|) when the omitted positions form a finite set F, and zero when infinitely many are omitted. When 0 is not in J and the value coded by J read as exponents is rational, the supported set is Lebesgue null, which closes positive measure selection over a rational fibre. The fair product measure on digit strings pushes forward to Lebesgue measure restricted to the achievement set, and the preimage of the rationals is null. Perfectness and nowhere density of subsum sets are classical after Kakeya (1914), and Kovac and Tao record the fixed base Cantor structure; the measure dichotomy and the rational fibre null theorem are the additions.
Six families give exact membership criteria for that set. GeneralRepairCriterion replaces a quantifier over supports by a pointwise inequality on one integer sequence: a nonnegative real lies in the set exactly when its greedy defect fails to increase at cofinally many scales, and when it fails to increase inside every window that starts at K and has width 2 times the integer square root of K plus 12. ScaledGreedyTrap identifies the set with the nonnegative reals whose scaled greedy remainder stays strictly below the barrier 2 at every scale. RationalMembership characterises a nonnegative rational target by infinitude of its skipped greedy ranks; PositiveSkipEquivalence and FourNinthsRepairWindows give the criteria at 1/2 and at 4/9; TwentyOneFatalBranch reduces membership of 1/21 to excluding one explicit fatal aligned branch. These are exact reformulations; they decide no target.
TerminalScaledVanishing and ActualUpperSuccessor state conditional refutations of the universal assertion: an unconstructed terminal scaled vanishing sequence of finite Boolean support words, or an unconstructed realised upper run lower envelope, each produces an infinite support of value exactly 1/2. Neither theorem places 1/2 in the achievement set.
Irrationality for an arbitrary infinite support is not proved, the memberships of 1/2, 4/9 and 1/21 are not decided, and the parent problem remains open.

candidates.title: RamanujanNestedRadicals: convergence and exact values of Ramanujan-type nested radicals
candidates.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the results of the author's paper "Nested Radicals of Ramanujan's Type with Arbitrary Coefficient Sequences" (Flamandzki, 2026). For a coefficient sequence a : N -> R, the radical of depth d is built by the recursion R_k = sqrt(1 + a_k R_{k+1}) from a seed; `Submission.rollUp a T d` is the depth-d truncation with seed T and `Submission.truncRadical a d` uses the seed 1. For a root order n >= 2 the square root is replaced by the n-th root (`Submission.rollUpN`) and, for the classical unbounded family, by the signed recursion with radicand (-1)^n + a_k R_{k+1} (`Submission.rollUpNS`), whose coefficients are a_k = altSum n (N + k - 1) for the alternating polynomial altSum n x = x^(n-1) - x^(n-2) + ... +- 1. Four statements are submitted: (1) for real N >= 2 and a_k = N + k - 2 the square-root truncations converge to exactly N (for N = 3 this is Ramanujan's radical; the statement is known, see the sources, and is the base case); (2) for every root order n >= 2, both parities, the truncations of the signed family converge to exactly N, which is not treated in the sources listed below (the only place where parity enters is the sign (-1)^n); (3) an arbitrary-profile theorem: if R_k >= 1 and the coefficients are the ones for which R satisfies the recursion exactly, R_k^n = 1 + a_k R_{k+1}, then the depth-d truncation with seed 1 satisfies 0 <= R_1 - T_d <= R_1 prod_{j<d} (1 - 1/R_j), and it converges to exactly R_1 whenever the sum of 1/R_k diverges (it contains every constant profile and the classical family for every even n, with an explicit rate; it is not stated in version 2 of the paper; version 3 states it). The development (`RamanujanNested/`, 24 modules) contains further results that are not advertised in `Challenge.lean`: boundedness and monotonicity, controlled negative coefficients, the inverse construction, the closed-form identity chain for every n, the constant-coefficient exact-target radical for every n, an oscillatory family, and existence of a limit for linear and prime coefficient families at every root order. The paper's numerical tables, algorithms as running code, and informal discussion are not formalized. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms.

candidates.title: The trace form of a tensor product of algebras and the signature product rule, with the trace forms of Q[x]/(x^3 - x - 1), Q[x]/(x^4 - x - 1) and their compositum as instances
candidates.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. For finite free algebras A, B over a commutative ring R, the trace form of the tensor product A ⊗_R B is the tensor product of the trace forms, and over a linearly ordered field the Sylvester signature of a tensor product of quadratic forms obeys a product rule. Seven compared general statements: (1) the trace of a pure tensor is the product of the traces, Tr_{A⊗B}(a ⊗ b) = Tr_A(a)·Tr_B(b); (2) the trace form on pure tensors is the product of the trace forms; (3) the Gram matrix of a tensor basis bA ⊗ bB (Mathlib's Basis.tensorProduct) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; (4) the discriminant product formula WITH SIGN, disc(bA ⊗ bB) = disc(bA)^|kappa| · disc(bB)^|iota| for bases indexed by finite types iota, kappa; (5) when 2 is invertible in R, the trace quadratic form of A ⊗ B is the tensor product (Mathlib's QuadraticForm.tmul) of the trace quadratic forms; (6)-(7) THE SIGNATURE PRODUCT RULE: over a linearly ordered field with 2 invertible, for quadratic forms Q1, Q2 on finite-dimensional spaces, sigPos(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 p2 + n1 n2 and sigNeg(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 n2 + n1 p2, with sigPos/sigNeg Mathlib's basis-free invariants (maximal dimension of a positive- resp. negative-definite subspace). (6)-(7) are the (p, n)-refinement of the multiplicativity of the signature homomorphism on the Witt ring of an ordered field (Lam 2005, Chapter VIII), stated for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) forms and proved by orthogonal bases and the uniqueness half of Sylvester's law. The Witt-ring statement gives only the difference p - n; recovering p and n separately for a possibly degenerate tensor product would in addition need the dimension of the radical of a tensor product, which Mathlib does not have either; the entry proves the two counts directly, without the Witt ring, which is not formalized. None of (1)-(7) was in Mathlib at the pin; Mathlib's nearest results are the trace of a tensor product of endomorphisms (LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct'), the determinant of a Kronecker product, the tensor product of quadratic forms and its polar form, orthogonal bases, and sigPos/sigNeg with Sylvester uniqueness — the infrastructure from which (1)-(7) are built. PRIOR ART on (4): Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow — for two linearly disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the discriminant of their compositum is |d1|^[K2:Q]·|d2|^[K1:Q] (via the different; the classical statement is in Khanduja 2019). Statement (4) is the elementary basis-level version: any finite free algebras over any commutative ring, the exact signed discriminant of the tensor basis, with no number-field, integrality or coprimality hypothesis; it neither implies nor is implied by the Mathlib theorem, and is cited beside it. THE INSTANCES (8)-(23), at the two fields cut out by the trinomials x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 — the cubic and quartic members of the family x^n - x - 1, irreducible over the rationals for every n >= 2 by Selmer's theorem (Mathlib), whose real roots above 1 are the plastic number and the quartic root of x^4 = x + 1 — and their compositum. The trace form of a number field K of degree n is (x, y) -> Tr(xy); in the power basis 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) its Gram matrix is the Hankel matrix (Tr x^(i+j)) of the power sums of the roots. (8)-(9) The Gram matrices, entrywise: Algebra.traceMatrix of the power family equals the explicit integer Hankel matrix — power sums 3, 0, 2, 3, 2 for the cubic and 4, 0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3 for the quartic, from Newton's identities on the coefficients. (10)-(11) The discriminants of the power bases, Algebra.discr of the same families: -23 and -283, both prime. (12)-(13) Explicit diagonalisations: the trace form, as a quadratic form, is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares with weights 3, 2, -23/6 resp. 4, 4, -9/4, 283/36 — one congruence among many, exhibited with its rational change of basis. (14)-(17) The Sylvester signatures as basis-free invariants: sigPos and sigNeg are 2 and 1 for the cubic trace form and 3 and 1 for the quartic, read off from (12)-(13) through Sylvester uniqueness. (18)-(23) THE COMPOSITUM: the tensor product L = K_3 ⊗_Q K_4 is their compositum Q(rho, Q) — the degrees 3 and 4 are coprime, so the fields are linearly disjoint and L is a field, statement (23), from Mathlib's coprime-degree linear-disjointness criterion — and (18)-(22) are the general theorems at this pair: Tr(x ⊗ y) = Tr(x)·Tr(y); the Gram matrix of the tensor power family x^i ⊗ y^j (Fin 3 × Fin 4) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; the discriminant of that family is (-23)^4·(-283)^3 by (4); the Sylvester signature is (7, 5) by (6)-(7) applied to (2, 1) and (3, 1) — agreeing with the classical (r_1 + r_2, r_2) for the compositum's two real and five complex places (context, not compared). The registered compositum entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 treats the same field as Q(rho·Q), through the degree-12 minimal polynomial of the product; that Q(rho, Q) = Q(rho·Q) follows by degree count and is context here, never compared. THE CLASSICAL SETTING of the instances: the trace form of a number field with r_1 real and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings has signature (r_1 + r_2, r_2) — for the Hankel form of a polynomial this is Hermite's 1856 theorem (the signature difference counts the distinct real roots), and for the discriminant matrix of a number field it is Taussky's 1968 note; Conner and Perlis's 1984 survey is the standard reference. Here (r_1, r_2) = (1, 1), (2, 1) and (2, 5), so the classical theorem predicts exactly (2, 1), (3, 1) and (7, 5), and the Hermite counts 2 - 1 = 1 and 3 - 1 = 2 match the real-root counts of the two trinomials. That general theorem is NOT formalized: the two-field instances are proved directly by explicit congruence, the compositum instance by the general theorems (1)-(7); the embedding counts r_1, r_2 appear in no compared statement. WHY THESE FIELDS, for the instances: the cubic field is the signature-[1, 1] cubic field of smallest absolute discriminant (LMFDB, sorted by |disc|: 3.1.23.1 first, then 3.1.31.1); its Galois closure is the Artin field of the weight-one newform 23.1.b.a = eta(z) eta(23z), the classical Hecke example with Artin image S_3, whose analytic conductor the LMFDB records as minimal among all classical newforms and whose Stark unit is the root of x^3 - x - 1 itself; its integral trace form — which the compared Gram matrix (8) is, the power basis being an integral basis — is the object of Mantilla-Soler's study of integral trace forms of cubic fields (Algebra & Number Theory 2010). The quartic field is the degree-4 member of the same trinomial family, registered as the degree-4 Mahler-measure minimizer (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), with the same profile: prime discriminant, monogenic. The field discriminants: the LMFDB records 4.2.283.1 (defining polynomial x^4 - x - 1, signature [2, 1], discriminant -283, monogenic, index 1) and 3.1.23.1 (reduced defining polynomial x^3 - x^2 + 1, the field generated by -1/rho, signature [1, 1], discriminant -23, monogenic, index 1) list -283 and -23 as the field discriminants; that the power bases are integral bases, so that the compared power-basis discriminants ARE the field discriminants, is cited from those records and not formalized; likewise the tensor power family is an integral basis of the compositum because the two discriminants are coprime (the standard integral-basis theorem for linearly disjoint fields; context only). PRIOR ART on the instances, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib contains no trace-form or discriminant computation for either field. The nearest prior work is the Lean 4 certification framework of Baanen, Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen (CPP 2025) and its 2026 sequel (Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen): they certify rings of integers, FIELD discriminants (as the determinant of the trace matrix of a certified integral basis) and, in the sequel, the signature (r_1, r_2) by real-root counting, for LMFDB entries at large; neither treats the trace form's Sylvester signature, and their published example sets (seven non-monogenic cubic fields unramified outside 2, 3, 5 in the first; the v1 example directory of the second) contain neither of the two fields here (checked 2026-09-02). Relative to that work, the compared discriminants (10)-(11) are the power-basis discriminants derived from the explicit Gram matrices — a weaker notion than the certified field discriminant, which coincides with it here because both fields are monogenic (LMFDB, cited) — and the Sylvester signatures have no counterpart there. The entry is not aware of a formalization, in any surveyed prover ecosystem, of the trace form of a tensor product of algebras, of the signature product rule, or of a number field's trace-form Sylvester signature. The proof modules descend from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

candidates.title: An Approximate Solution to the Minimum Vertex Cover Problem: The Salvador Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Minimum Vertex Cover has a classical linear-time ratio of $2$, and under the Unique Games Conjecture no polynomial-time algorithm achieves a fixed ratio below $2$ unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. We present version 0.1.4 of \textsc{Salvador}, a linear-time ensemble of seventeen strategies, numbered in the order in which they are computed: twelve base strategies (component amplification before a maximal matching, the maximal matching itself, degree and weight heuristics, reductions to auxiliary problems that are solved exactly, a decomposition into bipartite layers, a weighted subdivision reduction and a bounded-treewidth dynamic program), followed by five improvers (a union pass, local search, reduce-and-search, consensus forcing and a swap-maximize refinement). We prove that every strategy runs in $O((n+m)\,\alpha(n))$ time, and that the returned cover has at most $2\tau-r$ vertices, where $r$ is the number of components with an edge, so the ratio is at most $1.999999999$ whenever $\tau\le10^{9}r$. We prove exactness or a bounded ratio on several classes of graphs, among them every bipartite graph on which the Hopcroft--Karp phases of the layer strategy reach a maximum matching, and we give a per-instance certificate: a cover with at most $2L-|M|$ vertices, for a lower bound $L\le\tau$ and the maximal matching $M$, is within ratio $3/2$ on that instance. In a reproducible suite the returned cover satisfies $|C|\le2\tau-|M|$ on all $291$ tested graphs with a known optimum and is certified on the six without one, although single strategies violate it; on the $68$ DIMACS clique complements it is never worse than Hvala and optimal on $37$ instances against $18$. Whether $|C|\le2\tau-|M|$ holds on every graph is stated as a conjecture: a proof would give a linear-time $3/2$-approximation and would refute the Unique Games Conjecture unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$.

candidates.title: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
candidates.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(\Phi_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\le\theta<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>\theta$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-\theta)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $\theta=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.

candidates.title: Galois groups of Taylor polynomials: prescriptions and arithmetic families
candidates.abstract:
Let $f_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^n a_jx^j$ be the Taylor polynomials of
a power series with nonzero rational coefficients. We study
the proportions of degrees for which the Galois group over $\Q$
is symmetric, alternating, or neither. We prove that the set of degrees
$n\geq3$ with symmetric group can be chosen arbitrarily, even
for an entire function with positive rational coefficients whose
Taylor polynomials have distinct negative real roots. More precisely,
at each degree $n\geq3$ outside the chosen set, $f_n$ has exactly
one rational root, and the group on the other roots is the full
symmetric group.
Thus the proportions need not converge; when they do, the
proportion of other groups can be any number in $[0,1]$.
These conclusions answer negatively two questions of Katz and Rivin.
Moreover, for fixed $s\in\Q\setminus\Z$, we also give a condition on the
prime divisors of rational multipliers of the coefficients
$s/(s+j)$ that forces symmetric groups in density one.
For the Taylor polynomials of $(1-x)^{-s}$, we extend
Wei's eventual group classification to fixed number fields.
Over $\Q$, the number of exceptions to the symmetric group up to degree $X$
is $c_s\sqrt X+O_s(1)$, with an explicit constant $c_s\geq0$.

We also determine the groups of the central-binomial Taylor
polynomials in every degree and prove that every nonconstant
Catalan Taylor polynomial has symmetric group. This proves
Sun's Catalan group conjecture and his irreducible-reduction
criterion for the monic reciprocals of the central-binomial
polynomials.

candidates.title: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

candidates.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), none for the mathematics of (18)-(22), which is classical (the claimed contribution is the kernel-checked bridge from the registered Bedford-Kim family to the E_m Coxeter elements, for every m >= 4 (bridge) and every m >= 10 (spectrum, Salem) at once), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, the E_m Cartan matrices only through their entries, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums, Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange/List.prod, matrix literals, Matrix.map, spectrum, IsIntegral, Polynomial.aeval) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

candidates.title: Dimension growth, polynomial in the degree (Castryck–Cluckers–Dittmann–Nguyen)
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of the main results of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen, "The dimension growth conjecture, polynomial in the degree and without logarithmic factors" (Algebra & Number Theory 14, 2020), incorporating the authors' 2026 addenda. It proves uniform bounds, polynomial in the degree, for the number of rational points of bounded height on varieties over Q. The bounds are: projective dimension growth N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d^(2n²+5n−5) B^dim X for integral X ⊆ P^n of degree d ≥ 5 (Theorem 1); N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d⁴ B^(2/d) for integral projective curves (Theorem 2); N_aff(X,B) ≤ C(n) d³ B^(1/d)(log B + d) for integral affine curves (Theorem 3); and C(N) d^(3N+9) B^(N−2) for affine hypersurfaces whose top-degree form is absolutely irreducible (Theorem 4). It also proves the lower-bound construction d² B^(2/d)/5 (Proposition 5), and the 2-torsion bound h₂(K) ≤ C(n) |disc K|^(1/2−1/(2n)) (log |disc K|)^(1−n mod 2) for all number fields of degree n ≥ 3 (Theorem 6). Degree and dimension are defined through Hilbert functions of the coordinate ring. Every constant depends only on the ambient dimension or field degree. The proofs construct the paper's determinant-method, projection and counting arguments in full. They include corrected versions of several intermediate lemmas whose printed forms are false.

candidates.title: Classical theorems of Fröhlich and Spencer: the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition, massless phases of abelian gauge theories, and Anderson localization
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three papers of J. Fröhlich and T. Spencer (Communications in Mathematical Physics, 1981, 1982 and 1983), with the two-dimensional multiscale analysis in the finite-volume form of V. Kharash and R. Peled (2017). For the two-dimensional plane rotator it proves the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition: the two-point function decays exponentially at high temperature, while at low temperature it obeys the power-law lower bound of Theorem C and still tends to zero, so that there is no long-range order. The same multiscale expansion in charge ensembles gives the absence of screening and the power-law decay of fractional charges in two-dimensional Coulomb gases (Theorems A and B), the phase diagram of the Z_n clock models with an intermediate massless phase (Theorem 7.1), disorder bounds for the Villain model (Theorem D) and the roughening transition of the solid-on-solid model (Theorem 7.3), as well as the four finite-square theorems of Kharash and Peled. For the four-dimensional Villain U(1) lattice gauge theory at large beta it proves that the integer-valued dual gauge field has the exponential moments of a free massless field up to a renormalization of the coupling from beta to beta''(beta) with beta''/beta -> 1, in finite volume (2.93) and for every limit state along cubes; that a translation-invariant limit state has a field-strength correlation that is not summable, obtained as the limit of the finite-volume field-strength correlations, which is the paper's massless photon; the perimeter law of the Wilson loop at large beta and its area law at small beta; a perimeter law for the disorder operator of the Z_N gauge theories; and long-range order of the Villain XY model in every dimension D >= 3. For the Anderson tight-binding model on Z^nu at large disorder, or at high energy with Gaussian disorder, it proves exponential decay of the Green function with polynomially high probability, uniformly in the imaginary part of the energy (Theorem 1.2), its almost-sure decay, and the vanishing of the Kubo diffusion coefficient wherever the density of states is positive (Theorem 1.1). The FS82 statements are in finite volume or about limit points along cubes; the thermodynamic limits that the paper takes from Ginibre's inequalities are not formalized. Corrections to the printed texts are listed in the README.
