candidates.title: The additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair; Dixon, Theorem 1') and its representation-theoretic engine
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of the homogeneous case and, at the roots, of the printed form (relations with value in K), with coefficients in any field K of characteristic 0, of the additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair, Manuscripta Math. 39 (1982) 81-97, Proposition 4, Assertion 3, p. 86, for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|; stated by J. D. Dixon, Acta Arith. 82 (1997) 293-302, as Theorem 1', p. 301, with its proof omitted), of its representation-theoretic engine (classical: Huppert, Endliche Gruppen I, p. 597, Satz 20.2, as cited by Girstmair, Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 53-96, p. 78; used by Dixon on p. 297, in the proof of Theorem 1(ii), citing Curtis-Reiner Section 32B), and of two criterion forms over any field whose hypothesis is the irreducibility of the augmentation module instead of 2-transitivity (the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2, in its module form). Eight compared theorems, in namespace DixonRelations, in this order. (1) zeroSum_irreducible, the engine: for a finite group G acting 2-transitively on a finite set Omega with 2 <= |Omega| and a field K of characteristic 0, the augmentation (zero-sum) subspace V0 = {f : Omega -> K | sum_x f x = 0} of the permutation module Omega -> K is an irreducible K[G]-module; proved in the substantive form of simplicity, that a G-invariant subspace W <= V0 with W != bot equals V0. The G-action is the permutation representation (g . f) x = f (g^{-1} . x), and a subrepresentation is a Submodule together with an explicit invariance hypothesis. (2') additive_core_of_irreducible, the zero-sum criterion form: for any field K, any group G (finite or not) acting on a finite Omega, an injective family alpha : Omega -> L into a K-vector space L, K-linear maps phi g with phi g (alpha x) = alpha (g . x) (no homomorphism property assumed), and the hypothesis hirr (every nonzero G-invariant K-subspace of V0 is V0, word for word the conclusion of (1); it holds vacuously when V0 = 0, that is |Omega| <= 1), any c with sum_x c x = 0 and sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is 0. (2) additive_core, the zero-sum form for an abstract family: the same conclusion for K of characteristic 0 and a finite group G acting 2-transitively on Omega with 2 <= |Omega|; it is (1) followed by (2'). (3) additive_roots_no_relation, the zero-sum form at the roots: for K of characteristic 0 and an irreducible f in K[X] of degree >= 2 whose Galois group acts 2-transitively on the roots of f in the splitting field, any K-valued coefficient tuple c on the roots with sum_r c r = 0 and sum_r c r . r = 0 is 0; G = f.Gal, Omega = f.rootSet f.SplittingField (with Mathlib's instance Polynomial.Gal.galActionAux), the family is the inclusion of the root set, phi g is the field automorphism g read as a K-linear map (the compatibility holds by rfl), and 2 <= |Omega| follows from card_rootSet_eq_natDegree with separability from Irreducible.separable; f.SplittingField appears in the 2-transitivity hypothesis and in the types of c and of the relation hypothesis. (3) is the zero-sum part (value 0, coefficient sum 0) of the homogeneous case of Dixon's Theorem 1' at the roots; the full homogeneous case at the roots is (5), and the inhomogeneous case is (6). (4') relModule_le_span_one_of_irreducible, the span-one criterion form: under the hypotheses of (2') and a transitive action, every coefficient tuple c with sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is a scalar multiple of the all-ones tuple, i.e. relModule K alpha is contained in the line K . (fun _ => 1). This is the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2 (p. 86: "If G is primitive on G/H, (G,H) admits only trivial relations over K iff the complementary module U(G/H) of K epsilon_0 is simple"), whose hypothesis is, like hirr, the simplicity of a module; Girstmair 1999 restates it in character form as Proposition 12 (p. 78), "essentially contained in Proposition 4 of [11]". (4') assumes transitivity in place of primitivity; for a transitive action, hirr already forces primitivity (elementary, not formalized: the zero-sum functions constant on the blocks of a nontrivial block system form a nonzero proper invariant subspace of V0), so the difference is one of form only. (4) relModule_le_span_one, the span-one form: the same conclusion under the hypotheses of (2); it is (1) followed by (4'). (5) relModule_roots_le_span_one, the span-one form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), relModule K of the root family (fun r => (r : f.SplittingField)) is contained in K . (fun _ => 1); it is (4) at the roots. (6) roots_inhomogeneous_iff_const, Dixon's printed form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), sum_r c r . r = algebraMap K f.SplittingField k for some k in K if and only if c is constant; in Dixon's notation this is U = K.e. Dixon's Theorem 1' is stated for any subfield K of C and for relations with value in K; compared statements (2), (3), (4) and (5) concern its homogeneous case (value 0) and (6) its printed form (value in K), for every field K of characteristic 0, and (2') and (4') take any field. Girstmair 1982 states the additive theorem for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|, so characteristic 0 is a sub-case of his hypothesis; (2') and (4') take any field, but their content is carried by hirr, which this entry proves only in characteristic 0 and only for 2-transitive actions, as (1). An uncompared bridge, BDS.isAtom_zeroSumSubrep_iff, shows that hirr together with V0 != bot is atomicity of V0 in Mathlib's lattice of subrepresentations of the permutation representation on Omega -> K. (1) is proved by an elementary, character-free stabilizer-averaging argument; Dixon (p. 297) cites Curtis-Reiner Section 32B for the statement only; Curtis-Reiner was not consulted, and nothing is claimed about its proof. (2') applies hirr to relModule K alpha meet V0 and uses injectivity of alpha; (4') shows that a relation and each of its translates differ by a zero-sum relation, so the relation is G-invariant, hence constant by transitivity (no averaging); the forward direction of (6) argues in the same way at the roots for a relation with value in K, using (2), and its reverse direction uses that the sum of the roots of a separable polynomial is fixed by every automorphism of the splitting field, which is Galois over K, and so lies in K. This formalizes classical results; it is not new mathematics. Research context: additive and multiplicative relations among conjugate algebraic numbers are studied in Girstmair (1982, 1999), Smyth (1986), Drmota-Skalba (1991), Baron-Drmota-Skalba (1995), Dixon (1997) and Zheng (2021); in the sources read for this entry the doubly transitive additive case is derived from the criterion and character theory in one sentence (Girstmair 1982, p. 86), set aside because the doubly transitive pairs are classified (Girstmair 1999, p. 78), and stated with its proof omitted (Dixon 1997, p. 301); this entry gives a complete, character-free, machine-checked proof. The namespace BDS of the two entry definitions is the development's historical name (after Baron-Drmota-Skalba); no result of Baron-Drmota-Skalba is formalized. Formalization status (search of 2026-10-28 for the six statements (1), (2'), (2), (3), (4') and (4) as stated here, at the repository heads listed in README.md; a search result, not a guarantee): none of the six statements searched was found in any prover; (5) and (6), searched for on 2026-10-29 at the repository heads listed in README.md, were not found either. The fact behind the reverse direction of (6), that the sum of the roots lies in the base field, is in Mathlib at the pin in Vieta form (Polynomial.Splits.nextCoeff_eq_neg_sum_roots_mul_leadingCoeff), for the multiset of roots. The S_n case of (1) is formalized in augmentation form over every field in which |Omega| != 0 (every field when |Omega| = 2), in particular over Q, in TauCeti (TauCeti.isIrreducible_standardRepresentation, since 2026-08-05) and as Specht-module irreducibility over C in openai/math; the general 2-transitive case of (1) is formalized in character form over C in AxiomMath/CFSG (CFSG.permutation_character_orbit_count, public since 2026-10-27), the closest item found: CFSG also defines the same V0 over C under the same action (CFSG.Wreathed.CentralSL2.sumZeroSubrep) and computes its character, from which the C case of (1) in submodule form would follow in a few lines, but no theorem stating it was found. NOT formalized and NOT claimed: the MULTIPLICATIVE theorem (Dixon Theorem 1(ii), and, per Zheng 2021, arXiv:1912.07202v1, p. 2, Baron-Drmota-Skalba 1995, Theorem 3), under which 2-transitivity does NOT force triviality: for a prime p and b in Q not a p-th power, X^p - b has Galois group AGL(1,p) over Q, acting sharply 2-transitively on the roots, and the ratios of its roots are p-th roots of unity, nontrivial multiplicative relations; Dixon's Theorem 1(ii) gives necessary conditions for that exception; none of that multiplicative content is proved or claimed here. The additive theorem carries no such exception, because the additive module cannot contain any e_gamma - e_delta (Dixon, p. 301). Also not formalized: the 2-transitivity of any particular Galois group (a hypothesis in (1), (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6)); any case of hirr other than the 2-transitive one, (1); the imprimitive case (Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 1; Girstmair 1999, Proposition 12, first sentence) and the fact that hirr forces primitivity for a transitive action; the 'only if' direction of the criterion, the character form of its hypothesis, and the converse of Assertion 3 that Girstmair 1982 states for a splitting field; and the identification of Omega -> K with the scalar extension of Omega -> Q.

candidates.title: Hermite's signature theorem and the coprime compositum, with the degree-12 compositum of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six general theorems and twelve statements about one number field. General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). The field: the compositum L of Q(rho) and Q(Q), rho and Q roots of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1, built as the tower K3 = Q[X]/(X^3 - X - 1), L = K3[Y]/(Y^4 - Y - 1), of degree 12: (7) the setting (degrees 3, 4, 12; linearly disjoint sectors); (8) O_{Q(rho)} = Z[rho], O_{Q(Q)} = Z[Q], discriminants -23 and -283, O_L = Z[rho, Q] with basis rho^i Q^j; (9) d_L = (-23)^4 (-283)^3 = -6342648595267; (10) places (1,1), (2,1), (2,5) and the trace-form type (7,5) of L, derived from (2) and (3) with no root located; (11) the relative traces on the product basis; (12) Tr(-alpha^-1) = 1 for alpha^n = alpha + 1 in degree n, the unit sections -Q^-1 and -rho^-1 of the relative traces, their surjectivity on rings of integers and the integral splittings of ranks 3 + 9 and 4 + 8; (13) the orthogonal decompositions of L along the two sectors, with restrictions 4 Tr and 3 Tr of types (2,1), (3,1) and complements of types (5,4), (4,4); (14) the covolume 2^-5 23^2 283 sqrt(283) of O_L in Mathlib's normalization, which is 4 times the product covol(O_{Q(rho)})^4 covol(O_{Q(Q)})^3; (15) the discriminant -23^4 53^2 283^3 of the degree-12 polynomial, which is the minimal polynomial of rho Q, and the index [O_L : Z[rho Q]] = 53; (16) the subfield lattice {Q, Q(rho), Q(Q), L}; (17) root-rigidity and circle-freeness of L; (18) Smyth's lower bound for the Mahler measure on O_L, with Smyth's theorem as an explicit hypothesis (cited, not proved). Eighteen compared theorems. The mathematics of (1)-(6) is classical and no novelty is claimed for it; the contribution is the kernel-checked proofs: (1), (2) and (5) from Mathlib's sigPos, sigNeg (D. Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

candidates.title: Steinhaus Piercing with Slack: The Exact Asymptotic Constant
candidates.abstract: Let s(d) be the largest order N for which the first n + d points of a sequence in [0,1) meet every uniform n-cell for all n ≤ N. We prove s(d) = d/(1 − log 2) + O(√d), determining the limit asked for by Anholcer et al. and disproving their conjectured coefficient. For strong piercing, which requires meeting every interval of length 1/n, we obtain an exact finite harmonic capacity and rational constructions. A Dirichlet covering lemma and a packing estimate for disjoint gaps transfer the capacity bound to ordinary grids. We also solve the finite largest-gap minimax problem, establish rigidity for infinite heap refinements, and extend the asymptotic estimate to affine arrival budgets. Ordinary near-extremizers satisfy universal laws for root sizes and first-split times, with a corresponding entropy correction. An explicit finite obstruction shows why root constraints alone do not characterize ordinary piercing.

candidates.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
candidates.abstract:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.

candidates.title: Several complex variables: local theory, Hartogs phenomena, Weierstrass theory, domains of holomorphy and pseudoconvexity
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, on top of Mathlib, of the classical function theory of several complex variables on open subsets of finite-dimensional complex normed spaces, with values in complex Banach spaces wherever the statements allow. The compared statements cover: Cauchy's integral formula on polydiscs, Osgood's lemma, the equivalence of holomorphy and analyticity, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy estimates, the identity theorem, the maximum modulus principle, holomorphic dependence of integrals and the Cauchy-Pompeiu identity; the theorems of Weierstrass, Montel and Vitali and an estimate for holomorphic L^p classes; the holomorphic inverse and implicit mapping theorems; Reinhardt domains, logarithmic convexity, the characterization of convergence domains of power series, Laurent expansion, and continuation from Reinhardt and circular domains; Hartogs-Taylor expansion, Hartogs' continuity theorem, Hartogs' theorem on separate analyticity, removability of isolated singularities, the two Riemann extension theorems and Hartogs' extension theorem for compact holes; elementary analytic sets and their regular points; the local ring of analytic germs, Weierstrass division and preparation, and the Noetherian and unique factorization properties of the germ ring; injective holomorphic maps, Cartan's uniqueness theorem, linearity of biholomorphisms of circular domains, transitivity of the automorphisms of the ball and the inequivalence of ball and polydisc; holomorphic hulls, domains of holomorphy, Thullen's lemma, the Cartan-Thullen theorem and Bochner's tube theorem; subharmonic and plurisubharmonic functions, the Levi form, pseudoconvexity of domains of holomorphy, Levi's theorem and local peak functions; Runge domains and polynomial hulls. All results are classical; none is claimed to be new.

candidates.title: The Arithmetic of Time: chirality of the Padovan substitution
candidates.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate. These are the three compared statements of the registered record (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 at revision c48eb12), unchanged in this revision. The uniqueness results proved in this repository (Supplement.lean: padovan_minimal_unique, padovan_eigenvalue_unique, padovan_matrix_unique, pisot_ge_plastic, padovan_rules_chiral) are registered separately as PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 (stalex444/arithmetic-of-time-slowest-clock, revision 49eafbab4af8899b2a66469697bf74683a88ce87), which compares them over s, mir, inc and sub. Everything else in this repository is public and kernel-checked but not compared: among it the exact orientation threshold (padovan_exact_orientation_threshold_four), the irrationality of the distinguished slope (Time.beta_irrational), mirror identities for arbitrary substitutions, a rate identity, and the characteristic polynomial and chirality of a twelve-letter substitution for ρQ.

candidates.title: Almost all Markoff numbers are unique.
candidates.abstract:
A Markoff number is the largest coordinate of a positive integer solution of
$a^2+b^2+c^2=3abc$. Frobenius conjectured in 1913 that every Markoff number
is the largest coordinate of exactly one such solution with $a\le b\le c$.
We prove that the conjecture holds for almost all Markoff numbers: the
proportion of exceptions among the Markoff numbers up to $X$ tends to $0$
as $X\to\infty$.

Two such solutions with the same largest coordinate give simple closed
geodesics of equal length on the modular torus, that is, primitive homology
classes $v,w$ with equal values $N(v)=N(w)$ of the McShane--Rivin stable
norm $N$. Estimates for the boundary of the unit ball of $N$ reduce the
problem to the equations $N(Gv)=N(v)$ with $G$ a rational linear map. For
each $G$ that is not a symmetry of the torus, a zero-one law for the
$3$-adic analytic dynamics of the mapping class group on the Markoff
surface shows that the solutions $v$ have density zero.

candidates.title: Zero density theorems for short intervals
candidates.abstract:
Explicit zero-density results for the Riemann zeta function in short intervals, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib.  Count the nontrivial zeros whose imaginary part lies in a window (t-h, t+h], with multiplicity and with a zero on either horizontal edge counted for half.
Seven statements are submitted, and all seven are mechanically checked.  Two are zero-density bounds for the edge strip Re s > 1-alpha, valid for 0 <= h <= t^(2/3), proved by two different mechanisms -- Jensen's formula and Littlewood's lemma, the source's Theorems 2 and 3.  Neither dominates the other over the whole parameter range.  Two turn those into bounds on the fraction of the window's zeros lying in that strip, and are antitone in both h0 and t0, so one evaluation bounds every larger window: Corollaries 4 and 5.  The remaining three are the headline corollary, Corollary 1 -- for every alpha in (0, 1/6) there are h0 and t0 beyond which a definite fraction of the window's zeros, bounded below by an explicit POSITIVE constant, have real part in the middle band [alpha, 1-alpha], away from both edges of the critical strip.  One states it with the constant named, one with the constant existentially quantified as the source phrases it, and one at the explicit parameters alpha = 1/16 with a sharper radius, where the limiting constant is 9/25.
The positivity is proved, not assumed, and needs no numerics: every term of the constant except the leading one carries a factor 1/h or 1/log t, so it tends to a limit fixed by one rational inequality, which the radius 1/2 discharges for every admissible alpha.  The factor of two relating the two edge strips is the reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho), proved in the development to be a multiplicity-preserving involution of the zero set.
The results are conditional and their hypotheses are in the signature, not hidden.  They are of two kinds, kept apart in the development because a reader is entitled to weigh them differently.  Sixteen are published explicit bounds on zeta and Gamma transcribed from other authors; eleven are finite numerical certificates established outside Lean by arb ball arithmetic or mpmath on explicit compact boxes, which Mathlib cannot currently reproduce because it has no verified evaluation of zeta and the margins reach 9e-17.  The source's tables give the numerical values of the constant; they are not load-bearing for its sign.
`comparator.json` names exactly those seven and is the authority on what is checked.  Beyond them, the wider development supplies what they rest on: the Littlewood short-interval theorem (Theorem 32), the argument-integral machinery (Theorem 31), the appendix of explicit zeta bounds, the Laurent expansion of zeta'/zeta, and the reflection step.

candidates.title: Resonance-cluster analysis for a proposed counterexample to Fried's conjecture
candidates.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of the theorem FriedCrossing.fried_counterexample_of_resolvent_inputs, the machine-checked reduction behind a proposed codimension-one failure of Fried's identity ζ(0) = τ_R for acyclic characters on a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with b₁ = 1. For a simple illustration of the method with figures, see docs/counterexample_intuitive_view.pdf.
The Mechanism: Near (g_hyp, ρ_triv), along the conformal family g_τ = e^{−2τb}g_hyp with characters χ_θ, the Ruelle resonances near 0 form two small clusters: a rank-2 cluster in degree 1, encoded by a 2×2 matrix M(θ,τ), and a rank-4 cluster in degree 2, encoded by a 4×4 matrix A(θ,τ). A branch is one eigenvalue of a cluster matrix followed continuously in (θ,τ). Degree 1 has the closed branch and the twin s_nc(θ,τ), which starts at the double point s*(θ) < 0 and travels at rate r₀ > 0 towards 0. Degree 2 has the two locked branches (the same eigenvalues, lifted by d₀) and two pure branches, the roots of Q = X² − e₁X + e₂; the pure branch nearest 0 is z(θ,τ). At the crossing metric τ = σ(θ) the twin and z reach 0 together, the twin as a pole of ζ and z as a zero, so ζ stays regular at 0 and ζ(0; g_σ) = τ_R · (rate of the twin)/(rate of z). The twin's rate is at most 2r₀ and z's exceeds 2r₀, so ζ(0; g_σ) ≠ τ_R. Fried's identity would need the two branches to arrive at the same speed. The whole Lean argument is bookkeeping of these four branches.
What is Proved: The theorem is a conditional reduction. Its objects are two abstract resolvent families on Banach scales (structure fields = the cited facts: local uniform boundedness and two-sided inversion of the generator modulo inclusions, CDDP Lemma 4.3; smooth generator), complex structures, and nondegenerate frames; the cluster matrices M, A are DEFINED from them as real parts of the frame matrices A(p)⁻¹B(p) built from contour integrals of matrix elements of the resolvent. Its hypotheses are, in six groups, the properties of that data which the argument uses, each cited: (1) two independent states at s*(θ) in the degree-1 cluster at τ = 0, with s*(0) = 0, s* continuous, s*(θ) < 0 for θ ≠ 0 [DGRS (7.6), BuOl Cor 5.1, DFG Thm 2; independence = rederivation A2 of the informal account]; (2) the first-variation formula B·∂_τM(0,0) = diag(0,p) with r₀ = B_cc p/det B > 0 [CDDP (4.22), (1.3)]; (3) the degree-2 cluster at τ = 0 has spectrum {s*, s*, s*, −s*} [DGRS (7.6), k = 2]; (4) at θ = 0 the degree-1 cluster is singular and the degree-2 cluster has spectrum {0, 0, 0, tr M} [CDDP Cor 4.1, DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (5) every eigenvalue of M is an eigenvalue of A [DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (6) for any functions ζ₀, F, any τ_R ≠ 0 and dimension vector c: ζ₀ = F·z/s_nc off the crossing with F continuous and ζ₀(σ) = F(σ) at it [CD (6.5) at λ = 0], ζ₀ = τ_R wherever s_nc ≠ 0 [DGRS Thm 2 + Fried 1986], exactness of C₀¹ → C₀² → V₃ at each crossing [DR Thm 2.1], c₀ = c₄ = 0 and c₃ = c₁ [DGRS Lemmas 7.4, 7.2], c_k the dimensions. The conclusion: there are θ₀, δ > 0 such that for 0 < |θ| < θ₀ the twin crosses 0 at exactly one σ ∈ (0, 2|s*|/r₀], the ζ-order at 0 is zero, the zero branch has slope ∂_τe₂/e₁ of modulus > 2r₀, |e₁(θ,σ)| ≤ K₁|θ|σ, and ζ₀(σ) = τ_R · (pole rate)/(zero rate) ≠ τ_R, with the torsion identity of the zero cluster.
Dependencies: The identification of the abstract data with the geometry — that the resolvent families are those of the twisted deformed generator L_X + iθω(X) on the anisotropic spaces of g_τ, that ζ₀(τ) is the Ruelle zeta function of g_τ at 0, that τ_R is the Reidemeister torsion of χ_θ, and that the defined matrices are the cluster matrices (their imaginary parts vanish) — is the informal layer, taken from the cited papers and the accompanying note, and is not formalized. Nothing about manifolds, flows, anisotropic spaces or zeta functions is in Lean. Granting the six groups as cited, the theorem exhibits a counterexample to Fried's identity in the form stated by DGRS for acyclic unitary representations, at a non-generic metric where ζ is regular at 0 and zero-resonant states exist with cancelling multiplicities; the refined identity of CD Thm 4 holds there. Whether the six groups hold as cited has not been independently verified by a mathematician other than the author.

candidates.title: Cancellation of all ultraviolet divergences of quantum gravity by a scale-invariant gas of branes
candidates.abstract: A frozen Poisson gas of branes with no preferred size, each brane a layer of independent cells that shift the proper time of a crossing graviton, multiplies the graviton kinetic operator by an entire function without zeros, $\exp[\tfrac n2\Ein(\Box^2/M^4)]$ times a random factor that tends to a constant at high momentum, in almost every realization. We prove that for $n\ge4$ the theory of gravity built on it has no ultraviolet divergence at any order of perturbation theory: every graph with two or more loops converges, the one-loop poles are those of a local theory and are cancelled by three operators quartic in curvature with finite coefficients, Newton's constant and the cosmological constant do not run, the zero-point energy of the graviton is $3nM^4/(64\pi^2)$ for every regulator, and the physical $S$ matrix is unitary at every loop order. The propagator keeps the graviton pole alone, and the potential of a point mass is finite at the origin. A one-loop graph in closed form confirms the cutting rule and grows faster than any exponential of the energy, so the loop expansion is an expansion in a small parameter only below an energy between $1.4M$ and $1.9M$. The free Euclidean field is a Gaussian measure with finite curvature that is not reflection positive, which states what a construction beyond perturbation theory would have to supply.

candidates.title: Kinetic Aleksandrov estimates
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalisation of Aleksandrov maximum principles for kinetic equations d_t u + v.grad_x u - A : D_v^2 u = f in non-divergence form, with measurable, uniformly elliptic diffusion acting only in the velocity. For coefficients A(t,v) the estimate holds for every source exponent p > 2d+1; for autonomous coefficients a(x,v) in one space dimension for every p above a threshold 1 + beta_*(Lambda/lambda) < 4, where no exponent below 4 works uniformly in the ellipticity ratio; and for general measurable coefficients A(t,x,v) for every p >= 1 + 128 d^2 (Lambda/lambda)^2 / 3. In each case the estimate implies interior Hölder continuity of solutions; for coefficients A(t,x,v) this is the kinetic Krylov–Safonov theorem. The library also proves the parabolic Aleksandrov estimate of Krylov, the parabolic Harnack inequality of Krylov and Safonov, the terminal solution operators of the kinetic equation, and classical Dirichlet solvability on ellipsoidal cylinders. Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem is taken from the formalisation hoermander-rothschild-stein.

candidates.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
candidates.abstract:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.

candidates.title: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P²
candidates.abstract:
Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. Except for attributed third-party material, all text and code are AI-generated under Robert R. MacGregor’s direction. Robert is an amateur who welcomes collaboration (macgregor@gmail.com).

candidates.title: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds of Weil type for $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ with discriminant $-3$
candidates.abstract: Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$. We prove that the Weil classes of every polarized complex abelian sixfold of Weil type for $K$ whose Hermitian discriminant is the non-split class $[-3]$ are algebraic, and that every Hodge class on every power of such a sixfold is algebraic when its Hodge group is the full special unitary group. The proof starts from Galois covers of the projective line with monodromy group $W(E_8)\cdot\mu_4$, branched over twelve points: the multiplicity space of the natural representation in the cohomology of such a cover is the first cohomology of an abelian sixfold of Weil type, and a certified rank computation at one explicit cover shows that these sixfolds fill an open set of the nine-dimensional moduli space. Algebraic cycles reach these sixfolds through Milne's theorem on Lefschetz classes, from two sources: Schoen's cycles on cyclic covers, which a computer search shows do not suffice here, and products of determinant lines of characters on abelian covers of curves. For the second source we prove a general theorem (Theorem C): if such a product is of Hodge type at every Galois conjugate, and each of the cyclic covers involved has at least two branch points and order dividing $12$ after removing the common factor of its branch exponents, then the product spans a space of algebraic classes. Its proof runs Schoen's symmetric-product construction on each factor, localises at a special fibre, transfers to a product of Fermat hypersurfaces, and applies Shioda's theorem on products of Fermat varieties. This version is archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23566607; its computational certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23549514

candidates.title: Countable-coordinate factorization for compact products
candidates.abstract: Every continuous map from an arbitrary product of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces into a metrizable space factors continuously through a countable subproduct. A uniform-space proof establishes countable coordinate dependence for uniformly continuous maps into separated countably generated uniform spaces. The factor for a fixed coordinate set is unique. Countably many maps share a countable coordinate set. Continuous injections into metrizable targets force only countably many nontrivial factors, giving the exact metrizability criterion for nonempty compact Hausdorff products. Empty index and empty selected-coordinate sets are allowed. These are classical results and no novelty or priority is claimed.

candidates.title: Grushko--Neumann rank additivity for free products
candidates.abstract: Formalizes the binary Grushko--Neumann theorem: the minimal number of generators of a free product of two finitely generated groups is the sum of the minimal numbers of generators of the factors. The central theorem is proved by a kernel-checked finite labelled-graph reduction. For a minimal null path, the implemented reduction uniformly performs a source unfold, a subsequent safe fold, and an explicit monochromatic-vertex contraction; this gives the strict decrease used by strong induction and the separated-generator lower bound. The repository also retains the finite-core and free-group rank lemmas from the surrounding development as reusable supporting infrastructure, but only the global Grushko theorem declaration is selected by the public Challenge and Comparator.

candidates.title: Formalizing Delcourt–Postle’s refined absorption in Lean
candidates.abstract: One assembled Lean formalization of principal refined absorption results and their consequences. The selected results include refined omni-absorbers and refiners, labelled reserve matchings, dense compatible decompositions, an additive compatible-absorber interface retaining independence of the entire old ambient vertex set, and existence of simple designs for every fixed q > r ≥ 2 and index λ ≥ 1 at all sufficiently large admissible orders. The literal global embedding conclusion of the survey is refuted separately from a proved piecewise replacement. The research-note endpoints give completion avoiding an arbitrary forbidden partial Steiner system, sparse prescribed and finite embedded exact intersections, an initial polynomial intersection interval, and polynomial excess in partial parallel classes and Nash–Williams schedule rounds. Both external inputs are supplied by pinned proved theorems. The single comparison selects eighteen declarations from the existing aggregate proof root.

candidates.title: Optimal universal 1 → 2 qubit cloning at fidelity 5/6, the universal-NOT, and asymmetric cloning
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the optimal universal 1 -> 2 cloning of a qubit, with every figure of merit finite: a channel from one qubit to two is a finite Kraus family K_i : C^2 -> C^2 (x) C^2 with sum K_i^* K_i = 1 (the blank qubit is fixed, so this is a 1 -> 2 map; the Choi-Kraus theorem is not proved), the two clone fidelities of a pure input psi are Re <psi| Tr_2 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi> and Re <psi| Tr_1 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi>, and F1-bar, F2-bar are their averages over the six Pauli eigenstates (1 +- sigma)/2, Gaussian-rational density matrices (the six states form a 2-design, the octahedron being a spherical 3-design, so these equal the Bloch-sphere averages of Gisin-Massar, as Bowdrey-Oi-Short-Banaszek-Jones 2002, (11), print for qubit maps; that equality is neither used nor claimed). Theorems, kernel-only: for every channel (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 <= 5/6, so some unit psi has min(F1, F2) <= 5/6 (Gisin-Massar 1997, their largest-eigenvalue bound; Bruss-DiVincenzo-Ekert-Fuchs-Macchiavello-Smolin 1998 within the symmetric isotropic ansatz), proved by a six-term sum of squares in the Kraus entries; the Buzek-Hillery channel (1/6) V1 rho V1^* + (2/3) V2 rho V2^* (V1|0> = 2|00>, V1|1> = |01> + |10>, V2|0> = (|01> + |10>)/2, V2|1> = |11>; Buzek-Hillery 1996, (3.29)) is a channel whose two marginals are rho -> (2/3) rho + (1/6) Tr(rho) 1 (their (4.6); Werner 1998, (3.7)-(3.8)), so F1 = F2 = 5/6 for every unit psi (their root fidelity sqrt(5/6), p. 7); a channel with (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 = 5/6, or with F1, F2 >= 5/6 on every unit psi, is the Buzek-Hillery channel as a map (the uniqueness under the average-fidelity criterion is proved here from the certificate; Keyl-Werner 1999 prove uniqueness under the worst-case one-clone criterion Delta_one and Werner 1998 under the global criterion; the Kraus family and the dilation are not unique, Roubert-Braun 2008), so 5/6 is the greatest t for which some channel has t <= F1(psi), F2(psi) for every unit psi, in Lean's IsGreatest form; F1-bar, F2-bar >= 1/3 for every channel, attained for the first clone by the universal NOT on it with a maximally mixed second clone (the universal-NOT bound of Buzek-Hillery-Werner 1999 and Gisin-Popescu 1999, in six-state average form); the asymmetric trade-off a b <= a(a + 2b)(1 - F1-bar) + b(2a + b)(1 - F2-bar) for every channel and all weights a, b >= 0, also with worst-case fidelities in place of the averages (the largest-eigenvalue bound of Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf 2005, Section II, in every dimension, with their conic alpha^2 + alpha beta + beta^2 = 1 written homogeneously; Hashagen 2017, (6.4a); the curve of Niu-Griffiths 1998, (6.29); the conic of Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.31), and x^2 + x'^2 + x x' >= 1/4 of Cerf, PRL 2000, (6); Buzek-Hillery-Bednik 1998, (11); the full achievable region in Hashagen 2017 and Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021), proved by a sum of squares polynomial in a, b; the family (A0 rho A0^* + A1 rho A1^*)/(2(a^2 + ab + b^2)) with A0|0> = (a + b)|00>, A0|1> = a|10> + b|01>, A1|0> = a|01> + b|10>, A1|1> = (a + b)|11> (the optimal asymmetric cloner of Niu-Griffiths (4.13), Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.28), Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf (19), Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005 (27)) consists of channels with marginals rho -> (1 - b^2/s) rho + (b^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1 and rho -> (1 - a^2/s) rho + (a^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1, s = a^2 + ab + b^2, so F1 = 1 - b^2/2s and F2 = 1 - a^2/2s on every unit psi, with equality in the bound at the weights (a, b), and for a, b > 0 equality holds only for that channel (proved here; Hashagen's uniqueness is within symmetrized channels); a = b is the Buzek-Hillery channel; hence the square-root form sqrt((1 - F1-bar)(1 - F2-bar)) >= F1-bar + F2-bar - 3/2 (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (23)), its worst-case form, and equality along the family for a, b >= 0 (the curve of Niu-Griffiths (6.29)). For every channel 3(F1-bar + F2-bar) - 7/2 <= sqrt((3F1-bar - 1)(3F2-bar - 1)), binding also where a clone is below 1/2 (with the floor, the necessity half of Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021, Theorem 6, at d = 2 for the six-state averages; Hashagen 2017, Theorem 6.4, in entanglement fidelity), proved by a Gram identity in the Kraus entries and Cauchy-Schwarz, with equality along the family when (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0 and, with neither clone perfect, only there; a perfect clone on average leaves the other at 1/2 (Hashagen 2017, p. 20, via Nielsen 2002, (3)); the asymmetric bound holds for all real a, b with (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0, the family being its only equality case when the product is positive and a, b != 0, and at (3, -1) it is the anticloning bound 3F1-bar - 5F2-bar <= 1, attained only by asymChannel 3 (-1), at (13/14, 5/14); F2-bar = 1/3 forces F1-bar <= 5/6, and (5/6, 1/3) is attained only by asymChannel 2 (-1), on every unit psi, the Buzek-Hillery clone with its anti-clone (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (12)-(15)), and likewise with the clones exchanged; if (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 >= 5/6 - eps, the Kraus operators lie within total squared Frobenius distance 6 eps of span{V1, V2}, and ||Lambda(rho) - Lambda_BH(rho)||_F <= 200 sqrt(eps) ||rho||_F for every input rho. candidates.title: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application
candidates.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). (I) THE CLASSIFICATION OF RADIAL HARMONIC FUNCTIONS: (1) for n ≠ 2 and E ≠ 0, the radial function f ∘ ‖·‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) on (0, ∞) for some real a, b; (2) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r — every radial harmonic function with a twice-differentiable profile is an affine function of the Newtonian potential, constants included, and of the logarithm in the plane. (II) THE LAPLACIAN OF RADIAL FUNCTIONS, away from the origin: (3) Δ(f ∘ ‖·‖)(x) = f''(‖x‖) + (n − 1) f'(‖x‖)/‖x‖, the radial Laplacian; (4) for g twice differentiable on (0, ∞), Δ(g(‖y‖²))(x) = 2n g'(‖x‖²) + 4‖x‖² g''(‖x‖²), the squared-norm parametrization; (5) for every real s, Δ(‖y‖^s)(x) = s (n + s − 2) ‖x‖^(s−2), the indicial identity (its consequence, not itself compared: for E ≠ 0, ‖y‖^s is harmonic away from 0 exactly when s (n + s − 2) = 0, at s = 0 and s = 2 − n, which coincide at n = 2); (6) Δ(log ‖y‖)(x) = (n − 2)/‖x‖²; (7) ‖y‖^(2−n) is harmonic on E ∖ {0} for every n — for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin (the normalization and the distributional identity −ΔΦ = δ at the origin, in Evans's sign convention, which make a normalized multiple of it the fundamental solution proper, are NOT formalized); at n = 2 the power is the constant 1 and the logarithmic case is (8); on the zero space the statement is vacuous; (8) log ‖y‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} when n = 2. (III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. (IV) THE STABILITY OF CIRCULAR ORBITS, general in the real exponent: for the effective potential U(r) = a/r² − b/r^p on (0, ∞), a, b > 0, p > 0 real — the radial potential of a body with angular momentum under a central attraction with force law 1/r^(p+1) — (11) U'(r) = 0 iff r^(2−p) = 2a/(bp), the circular-orbit condition (for p ≠ 2 that equation has exactly one positive solution, whence "the circular orbit" below — a consequence of (11), not itself compared; in the plane "the circular orbit r = √(2a/b)" names the point of (19)); (12) at a circular orbit U''(r) = 2a(2 − p)/r⁴; (13) for p < 2 the circular orbit r* = (2a/(bp))^(1/(2−p)) is a local minimum of U (Mathlib's non-strict IsLocalMin) — stable; (14) for p > 2 it is a local maximum — unstable; (15) for p > 2 U has no local minimum on (0, ∞) at all (Ehrenfest's reading, that bounded motion between two radii is then impossible, is not formalized); (16) U''(r*) r*⁴/(2a) = 2 − p, the square of the ratio of the radial to the angular frequency of small oscillations about the circular orbit, which the local step of Bertrand's argument requires to be the square of a rational number for a near-circular orbit to close. The boundary p = 2, where the two terms of U have the same power, is covered by the critical-point and second-derivative identities (11)-(12), whose only hypothesis on the exponent is p > 0, and is excluded from the stability conclusions (13)-(15) and the frequency identity (16), all of which require p ≠ 2; among the instances it is n = 4, where (17) with a ≠ b yields no local minimum (the potential (a − b)/r² has no critical point) while the sub-case a = b, where U vanishes, is excluded; the table's 'unstable' cell at n = 4 is not compared. THE INSTANCES (17)-(23), with p = n − 2 for the Newtonian potential in n ≥ 3 dimensions and the logarithmic potential in the plane: (17) for n ≥ 3 and a ≠ b a stable circular orbit exists iff n = 3 (a ≠ b excludes n = 4, a = b, where U vanishes identically and every point is a non-strict minimum); (18) for n ≥ 5 the effective potential has no local minimum on (0, ∞); (19) in the plane, for a/r² + b log r, the circular orbit r = √(2a/b) is stable; (20) the quantity of (16) is 4 − n for n ≥ 3, n ≠ 4, hence 1 at n = 3; (21) in the plane it equals 2; (22) in the plane its square root is irrational (it is √2 by (21); this statement asserts irrationality only); (23) ‖x‖^(2−n) is harmonic on ℝⁿ ∖ {0} for every n; for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin, with the same disclosure as (7). THE APPLICATION: Ehrenfest's argument of 1917 (KNAW Proceedings 20 (1918) 200-209, §1 and Appendix I) that the stability of planetary orbits singles out three spatial dimensions. He deduces the n-dimensional force law from the Laplace–Poisson equation (the Laplace half is statement (7), harmonicity away from the source; the Poisson half, the point source, is not formalized; the classification (1)-(2) makes "the radial harmonic function" a theorem), reduces the motion to the radial equation ṙ = (1/r)√(A r² + B r^(4−n) − C²), and tabulates three columns — circular trajectories; motions between two positive values of r; motion to the infinite — for n ≥ 4 (unstable, impossible, possible), n = 3 (stable, possible and moreover closed, possible), n = 2 (stable, possible and not closed, impossible). Statements (17)-(22) are the extrema and frequency identities of the effective potential behind the first two columns for n ≥ 5, n = 3, n = 2 — a local minimum where the table says stable, no local minimum where it says bounded motion is impossible, the frequency ratio where it says closed or not closed; the passage from those identities to trajectories (bounded motion, closure, the third column), the n = 4 cell, and Bertrand's global theorem (1873) are not formalized. Tangherlini (1963) extended the argument to the n-dimensional Schwarzschild field; Caruso and Xavier (1987) and Tegmark (1997) discuss its epistemological status and call it Ehrenfest's argument, as does this entry ("Ehrenfest's theorem" names his 1927 quantum-mechanical result). NOT formalized: Bertrand's theorem, the third column and the n = 4 cell of the table, the derivation of the effective potential from the equations of motion, the relativistic extension, the wave-equation half of Ehrenfest's paper (Huygens' principle in odd dimensions), and any statement about the actual dimension of physical space — the theorems classify radial functions and a family of effective potentials; the reading that the stable case is the world we observe is Ehrenfest's, cited, not compared. PRIOR ART, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib has the Laplacian on inner product spaces (InnerProductSpace.laplacian, laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis), harmonic functions (HarmonicAt, HarmonicOnNhd, harmonicAt_congr_nhds) with complex-analytic examples — in particular AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_log_norm, which gives log |z| harmonic on ℂ ∖ {0}, the n = 2 case of (8) in the complex model obtained through complex analysis — the second- derivative test (isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos), the mean-value lemmas IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero and IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq, and real powers; it has no Laplacian of a radial function, no harmonic power of the norm, no classification of radial harmonic functions, no central-force mechanics, and no formalization of Ehrenfest's argument. No formalization of the classification of radial harmonic functions, of Ehrenfest's argument, of the harmonic Newtonian potential in general dimension, or of Bertrand's theorem was found in the surveyed prover ecosystems (Mathlib and its archive, the Isabelle AFP, the Coq Mathematical Components and Coquelicot analysis libraries). The proof module descends from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

candidates.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. candidates.title: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

candidates.title: A continuum whose hyperspace of regular subcontinua is homeomorphic to the irrationals
candidates.abstract:
For a metric continuum $X$, let $D(X)$ be the hyperspace of subcontinua of $X$ equal to the closure of their interior, with the Hausdorff metric. Camargo, Ordo\~nez and Ram\'irez asked whether $D(X)$ can be homeomorphic to the rationals or to the irrationals. We answer the latter question affirmatively. We construct a continuum $X\subseteq\ell^2$ as the closure of a countable tree of scaled copies of an indecomposable plane continuum. Two types of piece alternate: blocks with dense interior, and spines with empty interior carrying densely attached blocks. We characterize all regular subcontinua by nonempty convex sets of pieces satisfying a density condition, and prove that this coding is a homeomorphism onto a $G_\delta$ subset of a Cantor cube. We then show that no point of $D(X)$ has a compact neighborhood. The Alexandrov--Urysohn characterization yields $D(X)\cong\N^\N$, and hence $D(X)$ is homeomorphic to the irrationals. We also explain why this construction does not extend to the rational case, which remains open.

Github repository:
https://github.com/LucasAlves8Sp/A-CONTINUUM-WHOSE-HYPERSPACE-OF-REGULAR-SUBCONTINUA-IS-HOMEOMORPHIC-TO-THE-IRRATIONALS

candidates.title: Stark units for real quadratic fields and reciprocity laws
candidates.abstract:
We prove that every value of the arithmetic finite quantum dilogarithms constructed by Radchenko and Wheeler (arXiv:2609.21892) is an algebraic unit, and determine the Artin action for arbitrary quadratic pseudolattices. In particular,
the associated Stark units belong to the predicted ray class fields and have the predicted Galois action. We use finite Fourier transforms and distribution relations to obtain Frobenius congruences. We also give conductor bounds for individual values and obtain the unitary conjugates needed for Zauner's conjecture.

Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
