An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

candidates.title: The Real-Rooting Time Of Heat-Evolved Random Polynomials
candidates.abstract: Let $G_{n,t}=\exp(-\frac{t}{2n}\partial_z^2)G_n$ be a random Weyl polynomial of degree $n$ under the backward heat flow, with independent coefficients of a law that is not a point mass and has finite variance. Hall, Ho, Jalowy and Kabluchko showed that the empirical zero distribution collapses onto the real line at $t=1$. We show that the first time at which all zeros of $G_{n,t}$ are real, a finite-degree analogue of the de Bruijn--Newman constant, converges in distribution to $T_*=R_*^{-2}$, where $R_*$ is the smallest modulus of a nonreal zero of the random power series $\sum_j\eta_jw^j$ with coefficients of the same law; the convergence is almost sure under a coupling of the degrees that shares the top coefficients, whereas under the standard coupling the set of limit points of the real-rooting time is almost surely $[1,\infty]$. The proof rests on an exact count of the nonreal zeros of analytic combinations $\sum_{j\le n}a_jh_{n-j}$ of orthonormal Hermite polynomials: if the real power series $a$ has radius of convergence greater than $1$, no zeros on the unit circle and simple zeros in the unit disk, then for all large $n$ the combination has exactly as many nonreal zeros as $a$ has in the disk. Its method expresses the polynomial and its derivative in the bulk through a $2\times2$ matrix applied to $(h_n,h_{n-1})$, built from only $O(\log n)$ steps of the backward three-term recurrence, with the remaining terms controlled by a Christoffel--Darboux bound. For Gaussian coefficients the law of $T_*$ is a Fredholm determinant, $\mathbb{P}(T_*>t)\sim\frac4{3\pi}t^{-3/2}$ as $t\to\infty$, and $(t-1)\log\mathbb{P}(T_*\le t)\to-\pi^2/12$ as $t\downarrow1$, half of the constant for complex coefficients. At the scale $1/n$ the last pair of nonreal zeros collides inside the real bulk, at relative position $\cos\theta_*$, where $R_*e^{\pm i\theta_*}$ are the nonreal zeros of minimal modulus, and the real-rooting time is within $O(1/n)$ of $T_*$. In a window of size $1/n$ the polynomial is, up to a positive factor and $O(1/n)$, the model $\zeta\cos(\zeta+c)+\lambda\sin(\zeta+c)$, whose threshold for real-rootedness is given by Kepler's equation; the phase $c$ rotates with $n$, so $n(\Lambda_n-T_*)$ oscillates over an explicit interval and has an explicit limit law jointly with $T_*$.

candidates.title: Stability and Convergence of a Regularized Immersed Boundary Method under Dynamic Cartesian Refinement. Part I: Fixed Geometry
candidates.abstract: We analyze a conforming variational immersed boundary discretization of the two-dimensional unsteady Stokes equations with a fixed interface. Exactly divergence-free velocities are obtained from Cartesian bicubic Hermite streamfunctions; regularized surface moments impose the boundary condition, and backward Euler time stepping uses constrained orthogonal transfer. Arbitrary local fine-scale enrichments may be added or removed at every step while the complete coarse space is retained. For homogeneous interface data, a common coarse comparison family yields an exact energy identity, a physical no-slip defect of order (\sqrt{\varepsilon}+\sqrt{\ell}), and velocity convergence without a restriction coupling the time step to the number of mesh changes. We extend this analysis to a disk with prescribed time-dependent angular velocity. A coarse lifting reproduces rigid rotation exactly throughout every regularization support, independently of the refinement pattern and surface partition. Subtracting this lifting reduces the driven problem to the homogeneous constraint spaces with an explicitly controlled forcing perturbation. This gives driven stability, physical slip control, and a quantitative energy error estimate without assuming a uniform multiplier inf–sup condition. The method assumes exact integration and is not a standard staggered-grid AMR scheme. Manufactured unsteady stationary and rotating-disk calculations test the implementation and its quadrature sensitivity. General changes of interface geometry and fluid-driven rigid-body motion remain outside the analysis.

candidates.title: Selective normality and algebraic rigidity of multiplicative traces
candidates.abstract: A completely multiplicative sign function may be changed so that two quadratic traces remain identical at every index while a third becomes normal. We classify this freedom for the traces $n^2+1$, $n^2+2$ and $n^2-2$. After two traces and a finite prefix have been protected, a monic irreducible polynomial can be made normal from every prescribed source exactly when the field generated by one of its roots contains neither protected quadratic field. In the complementary case, every value of the polynomial is already fixed. A single decidable set of primes of relative density zero supports a continuous, relatively computable completion treating all admissible polynomials jointly, with uniform bounds for each fixed observation family. The proof combines weighted root counts with a sieve for moments whose order increases with the observation scale, followed by a selection using exact finite normalisers. We also give a sufficient condition on prime availability, explicit sparser reservoirs, and a divergent reservoir on which some sources have no completion with a convergent ordinary mean, despite convergence of all fixed word laws in probability. For larger protected families, the obstruction is governed by odd products of quadratic square classes. An explicit example distinguishes certificates for every numerical value from a rational norm identity in the variable.

candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked proof, for every Coxeter system on three generators a, b, c with m(a,c) = p, m(b,c) = q, m(a,b) = infinity and p, q >= 2, of the growth-series identity in the ring of integer power series: (sum_n a(n) X^n) * (1 - (X + ... + X^(p-1))(X + ... + X^(q-1))) = (1 + X)(1 + ... + X^(p-1))(1 + ... + X^(q-1)), where a(n) is the number of group elements of Coxeter length n; together with its instances (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf), (3,3,inf) and, for (2,3,inf) = PGL(2,Z), the sphere sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, ..., the Padovan identity a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, the two-sided bounds 2 rho^n <= a(n) <= 4 rho^n (n >= 2), and the growth rate a(n)^(1/n) -> rho, the plastic number, the unique real root > 1 of x^3 = x + 1; and, for the whole family, monotonicity and symmetry in (p, q), the growth rate of every hyperbolic member, and the minimality of the plastic number. Twenty compared theorems: (1) the general identity for all p, q >= 2; (2) non-vacuity, a Coxeter matrix of that type exists for all p, q >= 2; (3)-(5) the three instances; (6) the (2,3,inf) sphere sizes a(0..4) = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and the recursion a(n+5) = a(n+3) + a(n+2) for all n; (7) that the recursion fails one step earlier, a(4) != a(2) + a(1); (8) a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, for any sequence with the Padovan initial values and recursion; (9) existence and uniqueness of the plastic number; (10) the bounds; (11) the n-th-root limit; (12) monotonicity: a(n) of a (p,q,inf) system is at most a(n) of a (p',q',inf) system for p <= p', q <= q'; (13) symmetry in p and q; (14) 2 rho^n <= a(n), n >= 2, for every hyperbolic member; (15) for (p,q) != (2,2) exactly one tau > 1 solves (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1))(tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1; (16) a(n)^(1/n) -> tau; (17) tau strictly increasing in (p,q); (18) rho <= tau with equality exactly at (2,3), (3,2), so the plastic number is the minimal growth rate of the family; (19) tau < 2; (20) tau -> 2 as p, q -> infinity (for every sigma < 2 there is N with tau > sigma whenever p, q >= N). The family statements (12)-(20) give the growth rate of every hyperbolic (p, q, inf) group as the unique root tau > 1 of an explicit equation, strictly increasing in the labels, with the plastic number as the family minimum attained only at (2,3,inf) and (3,2,inf); they restrict to this family, and kernel-check there, Terragni's monotonicity (2016, Thm. A), Floyd's planar minimality (1992, p. 482) and the continuity of the growth rate (Floyd 1992; Yukita 2024). The mathematics is classical and no novelty is claimed for it: the growth series of a Coxeter group is rational and determined by its finite parabolic subgroups (Steinberg 1968; Humphreys 1990 Section 5.12); growth of planar hyperbolic Coxeter groups is Floyd 1992 and Cannon-Wagreich 1992, and the (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf) and (3,3,inf) sphere sequences are OEIS A096231, A179070 (shifted) and A054886, with generating functions derived there from Cannon-Wagreich Prop. 3.1 and, for A096231, the Padovan form a(n) = A000931(n+10) recorded; Floyd 1992 (p. 482) proves (2,3,inf) minimal among cusped planar groups and Kellerhals 2013 gives an alternative proof; Bucher-Talambutsa 2016 Prop. 18 proves statement (11) itself by a normal form and, with Mann's bound, the minimality of rho for PGL(2,Z) over all generating sets. The (p, q, inf) family is hyperbolic exactly when (p, q) differs from (2, 2); the affine (2, 2, inf) is included in (1). The contribution claimed is the kernel-checked general identity for all p, q at once, and the family statements (12)-(20) derived from it, from Mathlib's CoxeterSystem alone — Mathlib at this pin has no growth series, no exchange or deletion property and no parabolic-subgroup API — by constructing the amalgam normal forms, lifting their action to the group, proving Coxeter length equals normal-form length, and counting. No "first formalization" claim is made. Application, cited and not a claim of the entry: the (2,3,inf) group is the Weyl group of AE_3 = PGL(2,Z) (Feingold-Frenkel 1983) and, in the Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai billiard description of the Belinski-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz limit (a conjecture for generic singularities, Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 2.9), the reflection group of the billiard of 3+1-dimensional vacuum gravity near a spacelike singularity (Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai 2003 Section 8; Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 3.1), where a(n) counts the chambers reachable from the fundamental chamber after exactly n wall collisions over all initial data, so (10)-(11) give the growth rate of those outcomes (elementary reflection-group geometry, not formal content). Hypotheses are inline: the Coxeter system enters through Mathlib's CoxeterSystem with the three matrix entries as hypotheses, rho through its defining equation and 1 < rho, the Padovan sequence through its initial values and recursion; the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (CoxeterMatrix, CoxeterSystem, CoxeterSystem.length, Nat.card, PowerSeries.mk, Finset.range/Ico sums, Filter.Tendsto, Filter.atTop, nhds, real powers) — zero custom definitions. candidates.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. candidates.title: Classical theorems of Fröhlich and Spencer: the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition, massless phases of abelian gauge theories, and Anderson localization
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three papers of J. Fröhlich and T. Spencer (Communications in Mathematical Physics, 1981, 1982 and 1983), with the two-dimensional multiscale analysis in the finite-volume form of V. Kharash and R. Peled (2017). For the two-dimensional plane rotator it proves the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition: the two-point function decays exponentially at high temperature, while at low temperature it obeys the power-law lower bound of Theorem C and still tends to zero, so that there is no long-range order. The same multiscale expansion in charge ensembles gives the absence of screening and the power-law decay of fractional charges in two-dimensional Coulomb gases (Theorems A and B), the phase diagram of the Z_n clock models with an intermediate massless phase (Theorem 7.1), disorder bounds for the Villain model (Theorem D) and the roughening transition of the solid-on-solid model (Theorem 7.3), as well as the four finite-square theorems of Kharash and Peled. For the four-dimensional Villain U(1) lattice gauge theory at large beta it proves that the integer-valued dual gauge field has the exponential moments of a free massless field up to a renormalization of the coupling from beta to beta''(beta) with beta''/beta -> 1, in finite volume (2.93) and for every limit state along cubes; that a translation-invariant limit state has a field-strength correlation that is not summable, obtained as the limit of the finite-volume field-strength correlations, which is the paper's massless photon; the perimeter law of the Wilson loop at large beta and its area law at small beta; a perimeter law for the disorder operator of the Z_N gauge theories; and long-range order of the Villain XY model in every dimension D >= 3. For the Anderson tight-binding model on Z^nu at large disorder, or at high energy with Gaussian disorder, it proves exponential decay of the Green function with polynomially high probability, uniformly in the imaginary part of the energy (Theorem 1.2), its almost-sure decay, and the vanishing of the Kubo diffusion coefficient wherever the density of states is positive (Theorem 1.1). The FS82 statements are in finite volume or about limit points along cubes; the thermodynamic limits that the paper takes from Ginibre's inequalities are not formalized. Corrections to the printed texts are listed in the README.

The main result constructs global solutions and approximates the perturbed front by a phase evolving according to a viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation, with a uniform quantitative error bound.

candidates.title: Uniform permanence of endotactic reaction networks with measurable rates
candidates.abstract: Uniform permanence is established for finite endotactic reaction networks with arbitrary real complexes and measurable rate coefficients bounded above and away from zero almost everywhere. Each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains a compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set, with entry times uniform over compact sets of initial conditions and all rate histories within a fixed rate box. Global positive Carathéodory solutions exist and are unique, and an exponential continuous-dependence estimate holds for initial data under a common rate history on a compact positive region. The result resolves the Endotactic Permanence Conjecture stated as Conjecture 1.3 by Johnston, Pantea and Donnell (https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4662), using an ordinary-endotactic drift estimate together with the finite affine barrier construction from OpenAI’s work on weakly reversible networks.

candidates.title: Quantitative permanence and recovery with vanishing reverse rates
candidates.abstract: Quantitative permanence and recovery bounds are established for mass-action systems with vanishing reverse rates. For a finite weakly reversible network with rates proportional to powers of epsilon, eventual concentration bounds depend on the spread of the rate exponents, with geometric constants chosen before the individual rates. For an explicit three-species network, a prepared region admits global positive solutions with three distinct concentration scales. Every prepared solution reaches and remains in a smaller target by time (31/10)/(p^2 h^7), while an explicit prepared solution cannot enter before 400/(1313 p^2 h^7). Inventory inequalities give additional necessary restoration and depletion times from arbitrary positive initial states. A continuous reverse-exponent family retains arbitrary admitted prefactors and yields matching worst-case prepared recovery orders, together with exact common-clock transport, preparation identities and cumulative reverse-reaction bounds. Abstract constant-capacity and open-range state-dependent inventory comparisons are included without assuming monotone inventories.

candidates.title: Infinite rank of the three-prime running-LCM kernel
candidates.abstract: For pairwise distinct primes p, q and r, the three-prime reciprocal running-LCM kernel has nonzero square minors of every order, with row and column indices chosen independently of the third exponent. Consequently it admits no finite rational separated representation. The selected entry also proves an exact rank formula for threshold-column matrices, an explicit two-by-two example at 2,3,5, separation in the two-prime comparison, and the four-base dyadic recurrence for the actual 2,3,5 sum. A uniform finite-rank approximation statement concerns the rescaled carry matrix. The stronger unit-determinant modular minors are in E269_08 and are outside this configuration. Infinite kernel rank does not prove irrationality of the running-LCM series. In the selected rank theorem the determinants remain nonzero for every fixed third exponent k using the same injective row and column maps. The distance theorem concerns a rescaled real carry matrix and is not an approximation lower bound for the original summable kernel.

candidates.title: Curvature-Induced Killing at Stochastic Algebraic Folds
candidates.abstract: We study the lifetime of a regular algebraic branch under continuous forcing and infinite-activity tangent jumps. For a parabolic fold, a first-order tangent kick decreases the discriminant by an exact quadratic amount. Symmetric stable marks of index $\alpha\in(0,2)$ therefore generate a one-sided normal jump kernel of index $q=\alpha/2$, with a coefficient determined by curvature. The normal diffusion and jump amplitudes depend on the evolving tangential state. We compute the full killed generator on powers of the discriminant and obtain occupation and terminal-jump bounds for this same joint process. Uniformly subcritical normal drift gives finite censored boundary lifetime and finite cumulative killing rate; continuous contact and jump exit both have positive probability. At and above the uniform critical threshold, a logarithmic nonlocal barrier excludes censored boundary contact, and the original branch terminates at a jump almost surely. A comparison after a stochastic time change yields an explicit stretched-exponential upper bound for survival and hence all positive lifetime moments. In the subcritical regime, an optimized upper bound for the probability of jump termination tends to zero as the curvature coefficient or the initial discriminant tends to zero. The analysis combines power estimates for the jump generator with a logarithmic barrier at the critical threshold. Numerical calculations illustrate the dependence of terminal causes on curvature.

For every alpha in (0, 1/3) it constructs one divergence-free, Z^2-periodic drift b in C^0_t C^{0,alpha}_x intersect C^{0,alpha}_t C^0_x on [0,1] x T^2, and proves three properties of the advection-diffusion equation with this drift: anomalous dissipation of scalar variance for every mean-zero H^1 datum (Theorem 1.1 of the paper); a uniform C^{0,mu}([0,1]; L^2) bound by C times the H^1 norm of the datum along a set of diffusivities accumulating at zero (Remark r.LeBron.2); and non-uniqueness of vanishing-diffusivity limits for a class of data containing cos(2 pi n x_1) for infinitely many n (a corrected form of the paper's no-selection principle). The three properties are combined in one theorem, restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge. The formalization also proves existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and the classical facts the paper uses without proof.

candidates.title: Stability and Convergence of a Regularized Immersed Boundary Method under Dynamic Cartesian Refinement. Part III: Fluid-Driven Rigid-Body Motion
candidates.abstract: We study a conforming regularized immersed boundary discretization of the two-dimensional Eulerian Stokes–Newton system for one freely moving rigid body. Regularized interior moments complete the surface constraints used for prescribed motion. Positive excess mass and inertia define a fixed fluid–body kinetic inner product. A skew inertial correction is derived from the fictitious rigid interior; it has zero power but is necessary for the physical translational momentum equation. The method advances the body configuration with the preceding computed rigid velocity and then solves a linear joint fluid–body step on a dynamically enriched Cartesian space. Exact orthogonal transfer gives an energy identity independent of the number of mesh changes. Interior and surface moment defects control the discrepancy between the discrete background energy and physical kinetic energy. A volume-preserving geometry comparison and a moving coarse recovery family yield conditional joint convergence of the fluid velocity, rigid velocity, and body configuration on an interval with positive wall clearance. The error bound distinguishes the energy norm after geometry alignment from the generally weaker estimate at the same Eulerian points. The analysis assumes exact integration and explicit strong-solution regularity; it does not cover arbitrary density ratios or collisions. Manufactured coupled computations, independent residual checks, and a Lean algebraic companion document the numerical and formal verification scope.

candidates.title: Stability and Convergence of a Regularized Immersed Boundary Method under Dynamic Cartesian Refinement. Part II: General Prescribed Motion
candidates.abstract: We study a regularized immersed boundary discretization of unsteady Stokes flow around a rigid body with prescribed translation and rotation. The interface may change its position and orientation, while remaining uniformly separated from the outer wall. The fluid spaces are conforming, exactly divergence free, and constructed on fixed physical Cartesian grids with a retained coarse space and arbitrarily changing local enrichments. The method uses regularized surface-moment constraints, backward Euler time stepping, and current-space orthogonal projection. We construct a time-dependent coarse lifting that satisfies every discrete rigid-velocity constraint exactly. A moving collar approximation has a small spatial error in \(H^1\) and a small Eulerian time-derivative error in \(L^2\), although its time derivative need not be accurate in \(H^1\). This distinction permits a quantitative convergence proof without a restriction coupling the time step to the number of mesh changes. A shifted-interface trace estimate accounts for the motion of the reaction surface during each time step and for physical slip between time nodes. Under stated piecewise regularity and an \(L^2\) interface-reaction assumption, the energy error is bounded by the square roots of the retained coarse size, regularization width, surface-panel size, and maximum time step, together with a specified load-consistency error. The analysis assumes exact integration and does not prove adaptive optimality or cover fluid-driven motion. Manufactured moving-ellipse computations and a Lean algebraic companion test specified implementation and proof components.

candidates.title: Continuity, Testing Regions and Fragility of Quantum Channel Divergences
candidates.abstract:
Converse bounds on discriminating and estimating quantum channels are evaluated on a characterized model of the channels, which is only known approximately. This book studies when such bounds, and the operational exponents they bound, depend continuously on the channels, and whether their sensitivity to characterization error is a property of the task or only of the bound.

The book opens with noisy quantum gates. The supports of the Choi matrices separate genuine fragility, where the operational exponent itself jumps, from spurious fragility, where only single-letter converses jump. Near a gate with an incoherent noise floor, the smallest eigenvalue of the normalized Choi matrix sets the sensitivity. At first order, under errors in the model, this sensitivity belongs to the task. At second order, under a coherent miscalibration, the converses can overshoot the adaptive Stein and Chernoff exponents by factors that grow without bound as the noise decreases, although for small miscalibrations of a depolarized qubit they stay within a factor 3/2. Certifying a converse from tomographic data costs a number of channel uses set by the same floor.

The general theory follows. Divergences built from Kubo-Ando means, including the geometric fidelity, the geometric Renyi divergences and the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy, are functions of the Arveson-Radon-Nikodym derivative of one channel with respect to the sum of the pair, and in this coordinate they are continuous with dimension-free moduli. In the diamond norm they are continuous at a pair of completely positive maps exactly when the Choi matrix of the sum is invertible or the fidelity vanishes, so an ideal unitary gate paired with itself is a point of discontinuity. candidates.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
candidates.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.

candidates.title: Minimal recurrences for binomial power sums
candidates.abstract:
For every positive integer $r$, we prove that the least order of a
polynomial-coefficient recurrence for
$F_r(n)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk^r$ is $\lfloor(r+1)/2\rfloor$.
This establishes the unrestricted minimal-order assertion arising from
Franel's work of 1894--1895. We also determine the least order
$\lfloor r/2\rfloor$, for $r\geq2$, of the alternating sums
$(-1)^n\sum_{k=0}^{2n}(-1)^k\binom{2n}{k}^r$.
The lower bounds follow from real moment representations: every nonzero
singularity of the representing measure forces a root of the
leading characteristic polynomial of the recurrence. A common reflection argument gives
telescoping recurrences attaining both bounds. For the ordinary sums,
we combine the deformation of Straub and Zudilin with a shifted
prime-power congruence to prove that the minimal shift operator is
irreducible over $\C(n)$.

candidates.title: An FPT Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a fixed-parameter theorem of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all integer vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within 2^(c (p size(p) + 1)) (N size(M))^c bit operations, where p = gamma + k, N = |V| + |E| + 1, M = max(1, max |w_v|), size(x) is the binary length of x and c is an absolute constant; that is, 2^O(p log(p+1)) poly(N, log(M+1)) with an absolute polynomial exponent. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; orientable and nonorientable surfaces, disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The algorithm solves one exact linear program per retained component over a finite-group network whose size depends only on p, using exact integral quotient coordinates, midpoint convexity of class minima and a coarse Jensen inequality, and recovers an optimal set from perturbed edge costs. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

candidates.title: Hermite's signature theorem and the coprime compositum, with the degree-12 compositum of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six general theorems and twelve statements about one number field. General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). The field: the compositum L of Q(rho) and Q(Q), rho and Q roots of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1, built as the tower K3 = Q[X]/(X^3 - X - 1), L = K3[Y]/(Y^4 - Y - 1), of degree 12: (7) the setting (degrees 3, 4, 12; linearly disjoint sectors); (8) O_{Q(rho)} = Z[rho], O_{Q(Q)} = Z[Q], discriminants -23 and -283, O_L = Z[rho, Q] with basis rho^i Q^j; (9) d_L = (-23)^4 (-283)^3 = -6342648595267; (10) places (1,1), (2,1), (2,5) and the trace-form type (7,5) of L, derived from (2) and (3) with no root located; (11) the relative traces on the product basis; (12) Tr(-alpha^-1) = 1 for alpha^n = alpha + 1 in degree n, the unit sections -Q^-1 and -rho^-1 of the relative traces, their surjectivity on rings of integers and the integral splittings of ranks 3 + 9 and 4 + 8; (13) the orthogonal decompositions of L along the two sectors, with restrictions 4 Tr and 3 Tr of types (2,1), (3,1) and complements of types (5,4), (4,4); (14) the covolume 2^-5 23^2 283 sqrt(283) of O_L in Mathlib's normalization, which is 4 times the product covol(O_{Q(rho)})^4 covol(O_{Q(Q)})^3; (15) the discriminant -23^4 53^2 283^3 of the degree-12 polynomial, which is the minimal polynomial of rho Q, and the index [O_L : Z[rho Q]] = 53; (16) the subfield lattice {Q, Q(rho), Q(Q), L}; (17) root-rigidity and circle-freeness of L; (18) Smyth's lower bound for the Mahler measure on O_L, with Smyth's theorem as an explicit hypothesis (cited, not proved). Eighteen compared theorems. The mathematics of (1)-(6) is classical and no novelty is claimed for it; the contribution is the kernel-checked proofs: (1), (2) and (5) from Mathlib's sigPos, sigNeg (D. Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

candidates.title: Salem's theorem: every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked Salem's theorem — every Pisot number is a limit point of Salem numbers from both sides (R. Salem, Algebraic Numbers and Fourier Analysis, D. C. Heath, 1963, Ch. III, Theorem IV, p. 30; origin R. Salem, Duke Math. J. 12 (1945)) — with both of Salem's constructions, each stated as a construction. Three compared statements carry the surface. (1) salem_theorem — the theorem for Pisot numbers: a real algebraic integer alpha > 1 every other complex root of whose minimal polynomial has modulus < 1 (spelled as 1 < alpha, IsIntegral Z alpha, and every z in (minpoly Q alpha).aroots C other than alpha has norm < 1 — the spelling of the Pisot predicate in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, inlined) has, for every eps > 0, a Salem number in (alpha - eps, alpha) and one in (alpha, alpha + eps). (2) salem_construction_two_sided — Salem's main construction z^m P(z) ± z^p P(1/z) with its family root in the conclusion: for the pattern data of a monic integer polynomial P (one real root alpha > 1, every other complex root strictly inside the unit circle, conjugation-closed) under the nondegeneracy P(1/alpha) != 0 — a proviso that on the pattern domain is strictly STRONGER than Boyd's — coinciding, when P is the minimal polynomial, with Boyd's "provided P is not a reciprocal quadratic" (Math. Comp. 32 (1978), p. 1252, eq. (26)) and with the reason clause of Salem's, "so that Q and P will not be identical" (Salem's stated hypothesis, "theta not a quadratic unit", is stronger; fidelity (g)) — there is a sign e = ±1, the sign of P(1/alpha), such that for every eps > 0 some X^m P + e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some X^m P - e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps); P.reverse is z^p P(1/z), p = deg P. (3) salem_quadratic_unit — the excluded case, Salem's second construction (1963, p. 31) with its family root in the conclusion: for the reciprocal quadratic Pisot units alpha^2 = r alpha - 1, r >= 3 an integer, and every eps > 0, some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) + X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) - X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps) — the Chebyshev family (x - r) T_m(x) ∓ 1 pulled back through x = y + 1/y. Statement (1) is the theorem; (2) and (3) each carry their construction and neither follows from (1), their conclusions naming a root of a specific polynomial; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m" is NOT stated — (2) and (3) assert, per eps, the existence of some index m. A Salem number is spelled by Salem's definition of the class T (1963, p. 26): a real algebraic integer tau > 1 all of whose other conjugates lie in the closed unit disk, at least one on the unit circle — with the clause that 1/tau is a conjugate stated explicitly. Classically that clause and "degree at least 4" are consequences (Salem 1963, p. 26; Smyth 2015, Lemma 1); the equivalence is NOT formalized here, and the formal predicate is the stronger conjunction, which is the CONCLUSION of every compared statement — nothing is assumed of it. THE ROUTE: (1) is transported from a pattern-form theorem in the proof modules (salem_theorem_full), stated for any monic integer polynomial with the pattern data — a larger index set than the Pisot numbers (X^k times a minimal polynomial has the pattern) but equivalent in content, since the large root of any pattern polynomial is itself a Pisot number — through the bridge that the minimal polynomial over Z of a Pisot number carries the pattern data (the Gauss step: the minimal polynomial over Q is the rational image of the one over Z, since Z is integrally closed; separability of the irreducible minimal polynomial in characteristic zero; conjugation-invariance of integer coefficients). The pattern-form theorem splits on P(1/alpha) = 0: the nonzero branch is the assembly PdtSalemEndgame.salem_two_sided; the zero branch reduces to PdtSalemQuadUnit.salem_two_sided_quad_unit by a supporting lemma (reciprocal_quadratic_of_inv_root: a pattern polynomial vanishing at 1/alpha forces alpha^2 = r alpha - 1 with r >= 3 — the elementary "reciprocal Pisot implies quadratic", McKee–Smyth 2012, Lemma 6.2). Those two assemblies discard the index and the family; (2) and (3) are the same assemblies re-run in the bridge module SalemPisot with both kept. The book runs Case 1 under the proviso and handles the quadratic units in Case 2; the kernel unifies both cases in a single statement with no nondegeneracy hypothesis — a presentational unification of Salem's own two cases, not a mathematical strengthening of the theorem, which has no gap. The proofs use no argument principle and no Rouché theorem: the circle counts (m + p - 2 unimodular roots for the plus family z^m P + z^p P(1/z) with p = deg P, m + p - 3 plus the root z = 1 for the minus family, 2m for the quadratic-unit family) are intermediate-value arguments on explicit real phases; the trichotomy (every root unimodular or in {tau, 1/tau}) is a multiset squeeze against the degree; Salem-ness is an arithmetic certificate (the minimal polynomial divides the family; the Gauss step excludes degrees 1 and 2 and forces 1/tau a conjugate), with the integer degeneracies tau in Z and tau + 1/tau in Z discharged by finiteness along the ladders, or directly for the quadratic-unit family. NOT formalized: the equivalence of the Salem-number definitions (above); Boyd's converse (Boyd 1977: every Salem number arises from the construction); Salem 1944 (the Pisot numbers form a closed set); any rate of approach; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m". As of the 2026-09-01 sweep (Mathlib at the pin and at master, Loogle, the Isabelle AFP at title/abstract/filename level, Coq, HOL Light, Metamath, arXiv; GitHub native code search and Mizar not run) the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of Salem's theorem or of Salem numbers in any surveyed prover ecosystem; the one adjacent hit is the IsPisot definition in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (the definition and the golden-ratio instance; no Salem numbers), whose spelling the compared statement adopts. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

candidates.title: Erdős problem #257: all base irrationality of the reciprocal Mersenne subseries for every infinite reciprocal summable support, with weighted mass and positive cover extensions, achievement set geometry, and exact greedy membership criteria
candidates.abstract:
Erdős problem 257 asks whether the sum over a in A of 1/(2^a - 1) is irrational for every infinite set A of positive integers. The principal theorem compared here settles the whole reciprocal summable regime at every integer base: if A is infinite and the sum over a in A of 1/a converges, then the sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1) is irrational for every integer b at least 2 (ReciprocalSupport.irrational_supportPowerSeries_of_summable_reciprocal). No pairwise coprimality, periodicity, density, or powerful support hypothesis appears. Paul Erdős printed the pairwise coprime case of exactly this statement, at every integer base, in 1968, and stated there that pairwise coprimality can be removed by a longer argument he did not print. The theorem compared here is that stated extension, proved independently. No priority over Erdős is claimed and no identification with his omitted argument is asserted. The consequence for the parent problem is a boundary condition: any infinite support witnessing a counterexample has divergent reciprocal sum. Erdős problem 257 remains open.
The readers are number theorists working on irrationality for Lambert type and reciprocal Mersenne series, and analysts who study subsum sets of convergent series. Erdős (1948) proved irrationality of the full support value at every integer base; Erdős (1968) proved the pairwise coprime reciprocal summable case; Duverney and Tachiya (2019) treated the squarefree support at every base 2^j; Tao and Teravainen proved the prime support case at base two. Duverney and Tachiya record the Erdős and Graham conjecture that the sum is irrational for every increasing sequence of exponents and describe their corollary as support for it. Each covers one distinguished family; none covers an arbitrary reciprocal summable support, nor the reciprocal divergent supports below.
Three theorems state sufficient criteria that do not ask for reciprocal summability. Write h(a) for the P part of a at a finite nonempty prime set P. DivisibilityWeightedSupport.divisibilityWeightedClaim has two clauses: convergence of the sum over a in A of h(a)/(a(b^h(a) - 1)) at a fixed base b at least 2, for infinite A avoiding 0, gives irrationality at that base; the same weighted mass at base two on a host H avoiding 0 gives irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of H. VariableExponentCover.strengthenedPositiveCoverClaim gives that hereditary all base conclusion for every infinite subset of the host of a positive fractional divisor cover of convergent one inverse power cost, and MixedWeightedCover.mixedSupportClaim combines the two criteria on one observation scale. LiteralWeightedCover.exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host makes the weighted enlargement strict: a weighted host of divergent reciprocal mass admitting no strengthened cover, whose infinite subsets are irrational at every integer base at least 2. DyadicObservationSummability records dyadic averaging estimates for weighted observation masses.
FinitePeriodNoncollapse is exact finite support arithmetic: for finite nonempty F of positive exponents and integer base b at least 2, the reduced denominator of the sum over n in F of 1/(b^n - 1) is coprime to b, the order of b modulo it is exactly lcm F, and lcm F is strictly below that denominator once it is at least 2. RationalTailRigidity adds four necessary conditions on a hypothetical rational value p/(2^c v): an unbounded positive integer tail orbit with exact doubling recurrence, a sublogarithmic bound on zero windows of the divisor incidence coefficients, a reciprocal mass floor from the order of 2 modulo an odd reduced denominator when the reciprocals are summable, and a dyadic mass alternative. None contradicts a rational value. BooleanMobiusCarry gives exact coordinates: for an integer p and a positive natural q, a support avoiding 0 with some positive element and base two value p/q exists precisely when a positive square root bounded integer carry has Boolean Moebius normalised quotient. That characterisation permits finite supports, so it excludes no rational value.
AchievementSetGeometry and FairCoding describe the set of all subsums of that series at base two. For every set J of allowed digit positions the supported coding map is injective with compact nowhere dense range, the range is perfect when J is infinite, and the Lebesgue measure obeys an exact dichotomy: 2^(-|F|) when the omitted positions form a finite set F, and zero when infinitely many are omitted. When 0 is not in J and the value coded by J read as exponents is rational, the supported set is Lebesgue null, which closes positive measure selection over a rational fibre. The fair product measure on digit strings pushes forward to Lebesgue measure restricted to the achievement set, and the preimage of the rationals is null. Perfectness and nowhere density of subsum sets are classical after Kakeya (1914), and Kovac and Tao record the fixed base Cantor structure; the measure dichotomy and the rational fibre null theorem are the additions.
Six families give exact membership criteria for that set. GeneralRepairCriterion replaces a quantifier over supports by a pointwise inequality on one integer sequence: a nonnegative real lies in the set exactly when its greedy defect fails to increase at cofinally many scales, and when it fails to increase inside every window that starts at K and has width 2 times the integer square root of K plus 12. ScaledGreedyTrap identifies the set with the nonnegative reals whose scaled greedy remainder stays strictly below the barrier 2 at every scale. RationalMembership characterises a nonnegative rational target by infinitude of its skipped greedy ranks; PositiveSkipEquivalence and FourNinthsRepairWindows give the criteria at 1/2 and at 4/9; TwentyOneFatalBranch reduces membership of 1/21 to excluding one explicit fatal aligned branch. These are exact reformulations; they decide no target.
TerminalScaledVanishing and ActualUpperSuccessor state conditional refutations of the universal assertion: an unconstructed terminal scaled vanishing sequence of finite Boolean support words, or an unconstructed realised upper run lower envelope, each produces an infinite support of value exactly 1/2. Neither theorem places 1/2 in the achievement set.

These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

candidates.title: Salem's theorem: every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked Salem's theorem — every Pisot number is a limit point of Salem numbers from both sides (R. Salem, Algebraic Numbers and Fourier Analysis, D. C. Heath, 1963, Ch. III, Theorem IV, p. 30; origin R. Salem, Duke Math. J. 12 (1945)) — with both of Salem's constructions, each stated as a construction. Three compared statements carry the surface. (1) salem_theorem — the theorem for Pisot numbers: a real algebraic integer alpha > 1 every other complex root of whose minimal polynomial has modulus < 1 (spelled as 1 < alpha, IsIntegral Z alpha, and every z in (minpoly Q alpha).aroots C other than alpha has norm < 1 — the spelling of the Pisot predicate in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, inlined) has, for every eps > 0, a Salem number in (alpha - eps, alpha) and one in (alpha, alpha + eps). (2) salem_construction_two_sided — Salem's main construction z^m P(z) ± z^p P(1/z) with its family root in the conclusion: for the pattern data of a monic integer polynomial P (one real root alpha > 1, every other complex root strictly inside the unit circle, conjugation-closed) under the nondegeneracy P(1/alpha) != 0 — a proviso that on the pattern domain is strictly STRONGER than Boyd's — coinciding, when P is the minimal polynomial, with Boyd's "provided P is not a reciprocal quadratic" (Math. Comp. 32 (1978), p. 1252, eq. (26)) and with the reason clause of Salem's, "so that Q and P will not be identical" (Salem's stated hypothesis, "theta not a quadratic unit", is stronger; fidelity (g)) — there is a sign e = ±1, the sign of P(1/alpha), such that for every eps > 0 some X^m P + e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some X^m P - e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps); P.reverse is z^p P(1/z), p = deg P. (3) salem_quadratic_unit — the excluded case, Salem's second construction (1963, p. 31) with its family root in the conclusion: for the reciprocal quadratic Pisot units alpha^2 = r alpha - 1, r >= 3 an integer, and every eps > 0, some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) + X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) - X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps) — the Chebyshev family (x - r) T_m(x) ∓ 1 pulled back through x = y + 1/y. Statement (1) is the theorem; (2) and (3) each carry their construction and neither follows from (1), their conclusions naming a root of a specific polynomial; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m" is NOT stated — (2) and (3) assert, per eps, the existence of some index m. A Salem number is spelled by Salem's definition of the class T (1963, p. 26): a real algebraic integer tau > 1 all of whose other conjugates lie in the closed unit disk, at least one on the unit circle — with the clause that 1/tau is a conjugate stated explicitly. Classically that clause and "degree at least 4" are consequences (Salem 1963, p. 26; Smyth 2015, Lemma 1); the equivalence is NOT formalized here, and the formal predicate is the stronger conjunction, which is the CONCLUSION of every compared statement — nothing is assumed of it. THE ROUTE: (1) is transported from a pattern-form theorem in the proof modules (salem_theorem_full), stated for any monic integer polynomial with the pattern data — a larger index set than the Pisot numbers (X^k times a minimal polynomial has the pattern) but equivalent in content, since the large root of any pattern polynomial is itself a Pisot number — through the bridge that the minimal polynomial over Z of a Pisot number carries the pattern data (the Gauss step: the minimal polynomial over Q is the rational image of the one over Z, since Z is integrally closed; separability of the irreducible minimal polynomial in characteristic zero; conjugation-invariance of integer coefficients). The pattern-form theorem splits on P(1/alpha) = 0: the nonzero branch is the assembly PdtSalemEndgame.salem_two_sided; the zero branch reduces to PdtSalemQuadUnit.salem_two_sided_quad_unit by a supporting lemma (reciprocal_quadratic_of_inv_root: a pattern polynomial vanishing at 1/alpha forces alpha^2 = r alpha - 1 with r >= 3 — the elementary "reciprocal Pisot implies quadratic", McKee–Smyth 2012, Lemma 6.2). Those two assemblies discard the index and the family; (2) and (3) are the same assemblies re-run in the bridge module SalemPisot with both kept. The book runs Case 1 under the proviso and handles the quadratic units in Case 2; the kernel unifies both cases in a single statement with no nondegeneracy hypothesis — a presentational unification of Salem's own two cases, not a mathematical strengthening of the theorem, which has no gap. The proofs use no argument principle and no Rouché theorem: the circle counts (m + p - 2 unimodular roots for the plus family z^m P + z^p P(1/z) with p = deg P, m + p - 3 plus the root z = 1 for the minus family, 2m for the quadratic-unit family) are intermediate-value arguments on explicit real phases; the trichotomy (every root unimodular or in {tau, 1/tau}) is a multiset squeeze against the degree; Salem-ness is an arithmetic certificate (the minimal polynomial divides the family; the Gauss step excludes degrees 1 and 2 and forces 1/tau a conjugate), with the integer degeneracies tau in Z and tau + 1/tau in Z discharged by finiteness along the ladders, or directly for the quadratic-unit family. NOT formalized: the equivalence of the Salem-number definitions (above); Boyd's converse (Boyd 1977: every Salem number arises from the construction); Salem 1944 (the Pisot numbers form a closed set); any rate of approach; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m". As of the 2026-09-01 sweep (Mathlib at the pin and at master, Loogle, the Isabelle AFP at title/abstract/filename level, Coq, HOL Light, Metamath, arXiv; GitHub native code search and Mizar not run) the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of Salem's theorem or of Salem numbers in any surveyed prover ecosystem; the one adjacent hit is the IsPisot definition in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (the definition and the golden-ratio instance; no Salem numbers), whose spelling the compared statement adopts. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.
