candidates.title: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

candidates.title: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

candidates.title: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9). Those four are a copy of spacetime's: rho has a single expanding embedding in Q(rho), the real one, and the spectral projection maps the quartic sector onto them, carrying Z[Q] with its trace form unchanged, of Lorentzian type (3,1) (10). rho acts on them as a pure dilation by rho = 1.3247..., the same stretch in every direction (10). Symmetrically, the unit theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 needs exactly three, and those three are a copy of space's: Q(rho)'s real space with its form of type (2,1) unchanged, dilated by t = -1/q' = 1.3803... (8, 9, 10). Taken over all three embeddings of Q(rho) instead of the one expanding embedding, the form on the quartic sector is tripled: the factor 3 of statement (13) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012.
The clock needs one dimension; the ruler needs five. On Z[rho] the plastic inflation needs exactly one: the line, over a two-dimensional window at the complex place (8). The plastic substitution's control-point sets are regular model sets in this scheme, with Rauzy-fractal windows in C (Baake and Grimm 2020), and in the theory the line is time and its points are the ticks (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019). The coupling ruler rho Q, which generates the parent field (Q(rho Q) = K; statement (15) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, where Z[rho Q] has index 53 in the integers; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), needs exactly five, over a seven-dimensional window (9): one real and two complex expanding places, a dimension neither sector has.
The parent holds no circle, so every minimal scheme is forced. Off the parent, eigenvalues on the unit circle can change the count: a Salem inflation's circle eigendirections lie in the internal space and cost nothing, so it still needs only a line (5, 12), but multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity, n >= 3, needs exactly a plane, and every element of finite order n >= 3 needs at least one (6). The parent has none. No element of K other than +-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (statement (17) of PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012), so every inflation of the parent by an element other than 0 and +-1 is hyperbolic, needs exactly as many dimensions as it has expanding embeddings (a complex place counts twice), and has a unique minimal scheme (4, 9).

candidates.title: Binary Regression for BV Class Conditional Probability
candidates.abstract: In this article we solve the problem of binary regression when the class conditional probability is a multivariate function of bounded variation. We study the consistency of binary regression under a nonparametric sampling framework. Sufficient conditions are established for the convergence of the binary regression estimator, and quantitative error estimates are obtained. We further strengthen the analysis by introducing the assumption that the feature vectors possess a point density measure of bounded variation. Under this geometric regularity assumption, the expectation-based error estimate is replaced by a deterministic estimate, yielding deterministic convergence in the $L^{2}$ norm and, consequently, almost sure convergence. The analysis demonstrates that the geometric distribution of the sampling points plays a fundamental role in the approximation properties of the estimator. Although the analysis is carried out on the torus $\mathbb{T}^{m}$, the results extend to arbitrary bounded Lipschitz domains after affine scaling, embedding into $\mathbb{T}^{m}$, and zero extension. The point density measure framework provides a deterministic geometric perspective on binary regression and establishes a connection between sampling geometry, bounded variation, and convergence theory.

candidates.title: The trace form of a tensor product of algebras and the signature product rule, with the trace forms of Q[x]/(x^3 - x - 1), Q[x]/(x^4 - x - 1) and their compositum as instances
candidates.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. For finite free algebras A, B over a commutative ring R, the trace form of the tensor product A ⊗_R B is the tensor product of the trace forms, and over a linearly ordered field the Sylvester signature of a tensor product of quadratic forms obeys a product rule. Seven compared general statements: (1) the trace of a pure tensor is the product of the traces, Tr_{A⊗B}(a ⊗ b) = Tr_A(a)·Tr_B(b); (2) the trace form on pure tensors is the product of the trace forms; (3) the Gram matrix of a tensor basis bA ⊗ bB (Mathlib's Basis.tensorProduct) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; (4) the discriminant product formula WITH SIGN, disc(bA ⊗ bB) = disc(bA)^|kappa| · disc(bB)^|iota| for bases indexed by finite types iota, kappa; (5) when 2 is invertible in R, the trace quadratic form of A ⊗ B is the tensor product (Mathlib's QuadraticForm.tmul) of the trace quadratic forms; (6)-(7) THE SIGNATURE PRODUCT RULE: over a linearly ordered field with 2 invertible, for quadratic forms Q1, Q2 on finite-dimensional spaces, sigPos(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 p2 + n1 n2 and sigNeg(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 n2 + n1 p2, with sigPos/sigNeg Mathlib's basis-free invariants (maximal dimension of a positive- resp. negative-definite subspace). (6)-(7) are the (p, n)-refinement of the multiplicativity of the signature homomorphism on the Witt ring of an ordered field (Lam 2005, Chapter VIII), stated for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) forms and proved by orthogonal bases and the uniqueness half of Sylvester's law. The Witt-ring statement gives only the difference p - n; recovering p and n separately for a possibly degenerate tensor product would in addition need the dimension of the radical of a tensor product, which Mathlib does not have either; the entry proves the two counts directly, without the Witt ring, which is not formalized. None of (1)-(7) was in Mathlib at the pin; Mathlib's nearest results are the trace of a tensor product of endomorphisms (LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct'), the determinant of a Kronecker product, the tensor product of quadratic forms and its polar form, orthogonal bases, and sigPos/sigNeg with Sylvester uniqueness — the infrastructure from which (1)-(7) are built. PRIOR ART on (4): Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow — for two linearly disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the discriminant of their compositum is |d1|^[K2:Q]·|d2|^[K1:Q] (via the different; the classical statement is in Khanduja 2019). Statement (4) is the elementary basis-level version: any finite free algebras over any commutative ring, the exact signed discriminant of the tensor basis, with no number-field, integrality or coprimality hypothesis; it neither implies nor is implied by the Mathlib theorem, and is cited beside it. THE INSTANCES (8)-(23), at the two fields cut out by the trinomials x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 — the cubic and quartic members of the family x^n - x - 1, irreducible over the rationals for every n >= 2 by Selmer's theorem (Mathlib), whose real roots above 1 are the plastic number and the quartic root of x^4 = x + 1 — and their compositum. The trace form of a number field K of degree n is (x, y) -> Tr(xy); in the power basis 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) its Gram matrix is the Hankel matrix (Tr x^(i+j)) of the power sums of the roots. (8)-(9) The Gram matrices, entrywise: Algebra.traceMatrix of the power family equals the explicit integer Hankel matrix — power sums 3, 0, 2, 3, 2 for the cubic and 4, 0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3 for the quartic, from Newton's identities on the coefficients. (10)-(11) The discriminants of the power bases, Algebra.discr of the same families: -23 and -283, both prime. (12)-(13) Explicit diagonalisations: the trace form, as a quadratic form, is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares with weights 3, 2, -23/6 resp. 4, 4, -9/4, 283/36 — one congruence among many, exhibited with its rational change of basis. (14)-(17) The Sylvester signatures as basis-free invariants: sigPos and sigNeg are 2 and 1 for the cubic trace form and 3 and 1 for the quartic, read off from (12)-(13) through Sylvester uniqueness. (18)-(23) THE COMPOSITUM: the tensor product L = K_3 ⊗_Q K_4 is their compositum Q(rho, Q) — the degrees 3 and 4 are coprime, so the fields are linearly disjoint and L is a field, statement (23), from Mathlib's coprime-degree linear-disjointness criterion — and (18)-(22) are the general theorems at this pair: Tr(x ⊗ y) = Tr(x)·Tr(y); the Gram matrix of the tensor power family x^i ⊗ y^j (Fin 3 × Fin 4) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; the discriminant of that family is (-23)^4·(-283)^3 by (4); the Sylvester signature is (7, 5) by (6)-(7) applied to (2, 1) and (3, 1) — agreeing with the classical (r_1 + r_2, r_2) for the compositum's two real and five complex places (context, not compared). The registered compositum entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 treats the same field as Q(rho·Q), through the degree-12 minimal polynomial of the product; that Q(rho, Q) = Q(rho·Q) follows by degree count and is context here, never compared. THE CLASSICAL SETTING of the instances: the trace form of a number field with r_1 real and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings has signature (r_1 + r_2, r_2) — for the Hankel form of a polynomial this is Hermite's 1856 theorem (the signature difference counts the distinct real roots), and for the discriminant matrix of a number field it is Taussky's 1968 note; Conner and Perlis's 1984 survey is the standard reference. Here (r_1, r_2) = (1, 1), (2, 1) and (2, 5), so the classical theorem predicts exactly (2, 1), (3, 1) and (7, 5), and the Hermite counts 2 - 1 = 1 and 3 - 1 = 2 match the real-root counts of the two trinomials. That general theorem is NOT formalized: the two-field instances are proved directly by explicit congruence, the compositum instance by the general theorems (1)-(7); the embedding counts r_1, r_2 appear in no compared statement. WHY THESE FIELDS, for the instances: the cubic field is the signature-[1, 1] cubic field of smallest absolute discriminant (LMFDB, sorted by |disc|: 3.1.23.1 first, then 3.1.31.1); its Galois closure is the Artin field of the weight-one newform 23.1.b.a = eta(z) eta(23z), the classical Hecke example with Artin image S_3, whose analytic conductor the LMFDB records as minimal among all classical newforms and whose Stark unit is the root of x^3 - x - 1 itself; its integral trace form — which the compared Gram matrix (8) is, the power basis being an integral basis — is the object of Mantilla-Soler's study of integral trace forms of cubic fields (Algebra & Number Theory 2010). The quartic field is the degree-4 member of the same trinomial family, registered as the degree-4 Mahler-measure minimizer (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), with the same profile: prime discriminant, monogenic. The field discriminants: the LMFDB records 4.2.283.1 (defining polynomial x^4 - x - 1, signature [2, 1], discriminant -283, monogenic, index 1) and 3.1.23.1 (reduced defining polynomial x^3 - x^2 + 1, the field generated by -1/rho, signature [1, 1], discriminant -23, monogenic, index 1) list -283 and -23 as the field discriminants; that the power bases are integral bases, so that the compared power-basis discriminants ARE the field discriminants, is cited from those records and not formalized; likewise the tensor power family is an integral basis of the compositum because the two discriminants are coprime (the standard integral-basis theorem for linearly disjoint fields; context only). PRIOR ART on the instances, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib contains no trace-form or discriminant computation for either field. The nearest prior work is the Lean 4 certification framework of Baanen, Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen (CPP 2025) and its 2026 sequel (Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen): they certify rings of integers, FIELD discriminants (as the determinant of the trace matrix of a certified integral basis) and, in the sequel, the signature (r_1, r_2) by real-root counting, for LMFDB entries at large; neither treats the trace form's Sylvester signature, and their published example sets (seven non-monogenic cubic fields unramified outside 2, 3, 5 in the first; the v1 example directory of the second) contain neither of the two fields here (checked 2026-09-02). Relative to that work, the compared discriminants (10)-(11) are the power-basis discriminants derived from the explicit Gram matrices — a weaker notion than the certified field discriminant, which coincides with it here because both fields are monogenic (LMFDB, cited) — and the Sylvester signatures have no counterpart there. The entry is not aware of a formalization, in any surveyed prover ecosystem, of the trace form of a tensor product of algebras, of the signature product rule, or of a number field's trace-form Sylvester signature. The proof modules descend from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

candidates.title: Native Lean finite Nash equilibria
candidates.abstract: Formalizes finite strategic-form games with player-specific finite move sets, pure profiles, unilateral deviations, best responses, dominant strategies, and two distinct potential notions. Pure Nash equilibrium is defined over utility preorders by the absence of a strict improvement; weak-inequality characterizations are restricted to linear orders. The library names the one-way improvement condition a generalized ordinal potential and reserves ordinal potential for the standard bidirectional strict-sign condition. It proves a global potential-maximizer certificate for pure Nash equilibrium, the standard Nash/local-potential-maximum equivalence, and acyclicity of the better-response relation for the generalized class. The development also gives checked counterexamples and Prisoner's-Dilemma/coordination/matching-pennies/rock-paper-scissors examples. Its native mixed layer proves support equalization, Dirac transport, the normalized excess-map reduction, and the closed/compact/ convex/continuous finite mixed-profile geometry. It also proves general finite mixed-Nash existence on a common nonempty move type by connecting the native excess map to an attributed, kernel-checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or the first Lean proof of Nash existence.

candidates.title: Hermite's signature theorem and the coprime compositum, with the degree-12 compositum of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
candidates.abstract:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six general theorems and twelve statements about one number field. General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). The field: the compositum L of Q(rho) and Q(Q), rho and Q roots of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1, built as the tower K3 = Q[X]/(X^3 - X - 1), L = K3[Y]/(Y^4 - Y - 1), of degree 12: (7) the setting (degrees 3, 4, 12; linearly disjoint sectors); (8) O_{Q(rho)} = Z[rho], O_{Q(Q)} = Z[Q], discriminants -23 and -283, O_L = Z[rho, Q] with basis rho^i Q^j; (9) d_L = (-23)^4 (-283)^3 = -6342648595267; (10) places (1,1), (2,1), (2,5) and the trace-form type (7,5) of L, derived from (2) and (3) with no root located; (11) the relative traces on the product basis; (12) Tr(-alpha^-1) = 1 for alpha^n = alpha + 1 in degree n, the unit sections -Q^-1 and -rho^-1 of the relative traces, their surjectivity on rings of integers and the integral splittings of ranks 3 + 9 and 4 + 8; (13) the orthogonal decompositions of L along the two sectors, with restrictions 4 Tr and 3 Tr of types (2,1), (3,1) and complements of types (5,4), (4,4); (14) the covolume 2^-5 23^2 283 sqrt(283) of O_L in Mathlib's normalization, which is 4 times the product covol(O_{Q(rho)})^4 covol(O_{Q(Q)})^3; (15) the discriminant -23^4 53^2 283^3 of the degree-12 polynomial, which is the minimal polynomial of rho Q, and the index [O_L : Z[rho Q]] = 53; (16) the subfield lattice {Q, Q(rho), Q(Q), L}; (17) root-rigidity and circle-freeness of L; (18) Smyth's lower bound for the Mahler measure on O_L, with Smyth's theorem as an explicit hypothesis (cited, not proved). Eighteen compared theorems. The mathematics of (1)-(6) is classical and no novelty is claimed for it; the contribution is the kernel-checked proofs: (1), (2) and (5) from Mathlib's sigPos, sigNeg (D. Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

candidates.title: What Does the Refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis Mean for Learning Theory?
candidates.abstract:
Two recent works by OpenAI and Anthropic refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). They count the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF on $n$ variables in time $2^{n/(\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}}$. Many fine-grained lower bounds in learning theory rest on ETH and its relatives. We determine what the refutation changes for learning.

The answer is a locality principle: the new algorithms speed up learning when each labeled example constrains few bits of the hypothesis, and under the CNF form of the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis, which survives, the speed-up ends at $\Theta(\log N)$ bits. Three transitions make the principle precise.

Locality. Call a class with $N$-bit descriptions $\kappa$-local if each label depends on at most $\kappa$ description bits, as for quantized models on sparse data. Then proper PAC learning, exact version-space counting and sampling, and the halving algorithm run in time $\mathrm{poly}(m)\cdot 2^{o(N)}$ on samples of size $m$ for $\kappa=o((\log N)^{1/4}/\sqrt{\log\log N})$, and proper PAC learning at constant accuracy does so for $\kappa=o(\sqrt{\log N})$. At inverse-polynomial accuracy, proper learning of $\kappa$-local classes is equivalent to $\kappa$-SAT, up to a factor $2$ in the locality. Under CNF-SETH, consistency for binarized perceptrons on $O(\log N)$-sparse data needs time $2^{(1-\gamma)N}$ for every $\gamma>0$.

Accuracy. Exact empirical risk minimization, proper agnostic learning and the exponential mechanism reduce to tensor contractions over a truncated polynomial ring. As a consequence, the Sparse Max-SAT Hypotheses of Alman and Vassilevska Williams are false. At constant accuracy, proper learning is SAT parameterized by formula length. With quasi-linear PCPs this gives a $2^{N/\mathrm{polylog}\,N}$ lower bound under a length form of ETH, which replaces Gap-ETH for reductions of quasi-linear size. At accuracy $N^{-3}/8$, the Max-3-SAT Hypothesis forces time $2^{(1-o(1))N}$.

Treewidth. Exact inference in graphical models of bounded degree and arity takes time $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. On expanders this beats every elimination order and every structured DNNF. Under $\#$CNF-SETH, time $2^{(1-\gamma)\mathrm{tw}}$ is again necessary once a model may have $\mathrm{tw}^{O(1)}$ variables.

We also take stock of the conditional lower bounds of learning theory: which ones fall, and which ones survive on which hypothesis. The bound for training one ReLU loses its proof, because its hypothesis about Densest $k$-Subgraph on bounded-degree graphs is false. The next obstacle is a permutation problem. On difference vectors $e_i-e_j$, empirical risk minimization for real-valued halfspaces is weighted Feedback Arc Set, which the new algorithms do not reach.

candidates.title: Marton's conjecture (the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture)
candidates.abstract: A Lean formalization of Marton's conjecture, widely known as the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, together with its principal consequences. If A is a non-empty subset of an abelian group of exponent 2 with |A + A| <= K|A|, then A is covered by fewer than 2K^12 cosets of a subgroup of cardinality at most |A|; the same conclusion holds with 2K^9 cosets. For an abelian group in which mx = 0 for every x, with m >= 2, the covering number is m * K^(256m^3 + 1). Three consequences are also recorded: a finite set of small doubling in Z^D has a subset of at least K^(-34) of its size whose affine dimension is at most (80/log 2) log K; a map between finite groups of exponent 2 whose additive defects f(x+y) - f(x) - f(y) all lie in a set S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values; and a map that is additive on at least a proportion 1/K of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1)/2 points. The proofs are by an entropy method: one minimizes a functional of the entropic Ruzsa distance between two random variables and shows the minimum is attained at a uniform distribution on a subgroup, so the development also builds a substantial theory of Shannon entropy, entropic Ruzsa distance, and, for the bounded torsion case, a multidistance for m-tuples. The repository is a collaborative formalization project begun in November 2023; the mathematics is due to the cited papers and nothing here is claimed to be new. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the six deliberate holes in PFRPalomar/Challenge.lean.

candidates.title: The Law of Forgetting in Moments of Sato-Tate Measures: Invariant Tensors, Maximal Tori, and the Rank Law
candidates.abstract: For a compact group G with a finite-dimensional representation V, the moments of the character are, by a one-line argument, the dimensions of the invariant tensor spaces: <chi_V^m>_G = dim(V^{otimes m})^G. We call the passage from averaging over G to averaging over a maximal torus T the "law of forgetting": T-invariants only require weights to sum to zero, while G-invariants impose the additional invariance constraint. For the standard representation of SU(2) the two ladders differ by the exact factor F_k = binom(2k,k)/Cat(k) = k+1 (proved via the Temperley-Lieb non-crossing matching basis). The general forgetting factor admits a complete asymptotic F_k = c_V * k^s * (1 + gamma_V/k + O(1/k^2)), where s is the number of positive roots; both constants are given in closed form: c_V = |W| / (2^s <h_d>), a ratio of the Weyl denominator's lowest homogeneous term at the saddle to its Gaussian average, and gamma_V = (epsilon_T - epsilon_G)/2, whose inputs are the quartic term of -log|chi/dim V| and the next term of the Weyl denominator. The exponent s = (dim G - rank G)/2 is verified across six compact Lie groups (A_1, A_2, B_2, C_2, C_3, G_2) through the theorem F(1) = dim V (proved: weight multiplicities one, Schur's lemma), and the universal U(N) family gives the closed form F(N,k) ~ R_N k^{N choose 2} with R_N = (2/N)^{N choose 2} / G(N+1), G the Barnes function, identified with the reciprocal of a Mehta constant. On the arithmetic side, the master identity is verified on elliptic-curve Frobenius data; the two-copy test E x E versus E_1 x E_2 reads Schur's lemma directly from the second moment (a single number, 4 versus 2, separates isogenous from distinct copies); and the (lambda,lambda) pairing identity of Howe duality is identified with the Dirichlet coefficients of the Rankin-Selberg L-function, the N <-> k symmetry reading as convolution symmetry. A parallel shape fingerprint W = E[Y^2]/E[Y]^2 bypasses the heavy-tail divergence of the Jensen-gap functional J = E[Y]E[1/Y], with closed forms for twelve distribution families. All conclusions carry explicit status labels (proved / numerically anchored / identified), and every error found during the research is recorded with its correction in an appendix.

candidates.title: Resonance-cluster analysis for a proposed counterexample to Fried's conjecture
candidates.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of the theorem FriedCrossing.fried_counterexample_of_resolvent_inputs, the machine-checked reduction behind a proposed codimension-one failure of Fried's identity ζ(0) = τ_R for acyclic characters on a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with b₁ = 1. For a simple illustration of the method with figures, see docs/counterexample_intuitive_view.pdf.
The Mechanism: Near (g_hyp, ρ_triv), along the conformal family g_τ = e^{−2τb}g_hyp with characters χ_θ, the Ruelle resonances near 0 form two small clusters: a rank-2 cluster in degree 1, encoded by a 2×2 matrix M(θ,τ), and a rank-4 cluster in degree 2, encoded by a 4×4 matrix A(θ,τ). A branch is one eigenvalue of a cluster matrix followed continuously in (θ,τ). Degree 1 has the closed branch and the twin s_nc(θ,τ), which starts at the double point s*(θ) < 0 and travels at rate r₀ > 0 towards 0. Degree 2 has the two locked branches (the same eigenvalues, lifted by d₀) and two pure branches, the roots of Q = X² − e₁X + e₂; the pure branch nearest 0 is z(θ,τ). At the crossing metric τ = σ(θ) the twin and z reach 0 together, the twin as a pole of ζ and z as a zero, so ζ stays regular at 0 and ζ(0; g_σ) = τ_R · (rate of the twin)/(rate of z). The twin's rate is at most 2r₀ and z's exceeds 2r₀, so ζ(0; g_σ) ≠ τ_R. Fried's identity would need the two branches to arrive at the same speed. The whole Lean argument is bookkeeping of these four branches.
What is Proved: The theorem is a conditional reduction. Its objects are two abstract resolvent families on Banach scales (structure fields = the cited facts: local uniform boundedness and two-sided inversion of the generator modulo inclusions, CDDP Lemma 4.3; smooth generator), complex structures, and nondegenerate frames; the cluster matrices M, A are DEFINED from them as real parts of the frame matrices A(p)⁻¹B(p) built from contour integrals of matrix elements of the resolvent. Its hypotheses are, in six groups, the properties of that data which the argument uses, each cited: (1) two independent states at s*(θ) in the degree-1 cluster at τ = 0, with s*(0) = 0, s* continuous, s*(θ) < 0 for θ ≠ 0 [DGRS (7.6), BuOl Cor 5.1, DFG Thm 2; independence = rederivation A2 of the informal account]; (2) the first-variation formula B·∂_τM(0,0) = diag(0,p) with r₀ = B_cc p/det B > 0 [CDDP (4.22), (1.3)]; (3) the degree-2 cluster at τ = 0 has spectrum {s*, s*, s*, −s*} [DGRS (7.6), k = 2]; (4) at θ = 0 the degree-1 cluster is singular and the degree-2 cluster has spectrum {0, 0, 0, tr M} [CDDP Cor 4.1, DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (5) every eigenvalue of M is an eigenvalue of A [DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (6) for any functions ζ₀, F, any τ_R ≠ 0 and dimension vector c: ζ₀ = F·z/s_nc off the crossing with F continuous and ζ₀(σ) = F(σ) at it [CD (6.5) at λ = 0], ζ₀ = τ_R wherever s_nc ≠ 0 [DGRS Thm 2 + Fried 1986], exactness of C₀¹ → C₀² → V₃ at each crossing [DR Thm 2.1], c₀ = c₄ = 0 and c₃ = c₁ [DGRS Lemmas 7.4, 7.2], c_k the dimensions. The conclusion: there are θ₀, δ > 0 such that for 0 < |θ| < θ₀ the twin crosses 0 at exactly one σ ∈ (0, 2|s*|/r₀], the ζ-order at 0 is zero, the zero branch has slope ∂_τe₂/e₁ of modulus > 2r₀, |e₁(θ,σ)| ≤ K₁|θ|σ, and ζ₀(σ) = τ_R · (pole rate)/(zero rate) ≠ τ_R, with the torsion identity of the zero cluster.
Dependencies: The identification of the abstract data with the geometry — that the resolvent families are those of the twisted deformed generator L_X + iθω(X) on the anisotropic spaces of g_τ, that ζ₀(τ) is the Ruelle zeta function of g_τ at 0, that τ_R is the Reidemeister torsion of χ_θ, and that the defined matrices are the cluster matrices (their imaginary parts vanish) — is the informal layer, taken from the cited papers and the accompanying note, and is not formalized. Nothing about manifolds, flows, anisotropic spaces or zeta functions is in Lean. Granting the six groups as cited, the theorem exhibits a counterexample to Fried's identity in the form stated by DGRS for acyclic unitary representations, at a non-generic metric where ζ is regular at 0 and zero-resonant states exist with cancelling multiplicities; the refined identity of CD Thm 4 holds there. Whether the six groups hold as cited has not been independently verified by a mathematician other than the author.

candidates.title: Integrability of Liouville theory: the Kupiainen–Rhodes–Vargas proof of the DOZZ formula
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of A. Kupiainen, R. Rhodes and V. Vargas (Annals of Mathematics, 2020) that the three-point structure constants of Liouville conformal field theory on the Riemann sphere are given by the DOZZ formula of Dorn–Otto and Zamolodchikov–Zamolodchikov. The structure constants are defined probabilistically: for 0 < gamma < 2, cosmological constant mu > 0 and charges satisfying the extended Seiberg bounds, C_gamma(alpha_1, alpha_2, alpha_3) = 2 mu^(-s) gamma^(-1) Gamma(s) E[rho^(-s)], where rho integrates explicit power weights against the Gaussian multiplicative chaos of the Gaussian free field pinned on the equator. The formalization proves C_gamma = C_gamma^DOZZ, expressed through the Zamolodchikov function Upsilon_{gamma/2}, at every point of the domain where Gamma(s) is finite, and at every point including the poles for the unit-volume constant; and it proves that the probabilistic reflection coefficient, built from Brownian motion conditioned to stay negative and lateral chaos, equals R^DOZZ (Theorem 3.5). The theorems hold for every model of the field and chaos, and models are constructed. All prerequisites are proved: the construction, uniqueness and moment theory of Gaussian multiplicative chaos and the extended Seiberg bounds (David, Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2016); the BPZ equations for degenerate four-point functions and the classification of their real single-valued solutions by the Gauss hypergeometric function (Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2019); analytic continuation of correlation functions, tail estimates for multiplicative chaos, fusion asymptotics, the shift equations and the quotient argument. Errata found in the three papers, and the places where the Lean statements differ from them, are recorded in docs/ERRATA-AND-DEVIATIONS.md.

candidates.abstract:

General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

candidates.title: On Bounds for Reciprocal Sums and Residues in Collatz Orbits, and Their Consequences
candidates.abstract:
We prove uniform bounds for reciprocal sums and residue products along Collatz paths. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite nonrepeating shortcut path whose input states are greater than $1$, let $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ be the sum of the reciprocals of its odd inputs, and let $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ be its finite-path residue. Then

$\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}<1, \qquad \rho_{\mathcal F}<\frac{4}{3}. $

For the first-arrival trajectory of a terminating positive integer $n$, these inequalities give

$\mathcal R(n)<1, \qquad \rho(n)=\frac{2^{E(n)}}{3^{O(n)}n}<\frac{4}{3},$

where $E(n)$ and $O(n)$ are the division and odd-operation counts. More generally, when each odd value greater than $1$ is counted once, the corresponding reciprocal-sum and residue bounds hold for every forward orbit, without a termination assumption.

The proof combines verified finite height-delay records and residue bounds, canonical-block reciprocal estimates, and an exact finite count organized by gap brackets. Gap brackets, closely related to parity vectors, record the divisions by two between successive odd inputs and organize the finite counting argument; together with a related coordinate representation, they also yield exact formulas for reconstructing finite trajectories.

After taking base-$2$ logarithms, the bound $\rho_{\mathcal F}<4/3$ leaves an uncertainty of less than $1/2$ in the relation between the even- and odd-operation counts. Since these counts are integers, either count is determined exactly by the other count and the path endpoints. We obtain nearest-integer restrictions on the changes in $E$ and $O$ between adjacent integers, apart from explicit small exceptions, and prove that adjacent terminating integers of equal height have identical operation counts. Thus every equal-height streak lies in a single operation-count class.

We further introduce the charge $\lambda=E-2O$ and associated height and charge slice functions to study the persistence and eventual break of equal-height streaks.  We distinguish class records, which are the least starting integers attaining specified values, from delay records, which attain new extrema relative to all smaller starting integers. The resulting record theory shows that $\lambda$-delay records form a subsequence of the odd-count delay records, which form a subsequence of the common division-count and height-delay list. On the class side, the nonpositive charge-class records lie among the odd-count class records, which lie among the division-count class records, which in turn lie among the height-class records. The corresponding hierarchies also hold for first-arrival paths to a common endpoint $z$ when $z=1$ or when $z>2$ is nonperiodic under the shortcut map.

candidates.title: An improved zero-free half-plane for Hecke L-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
candidates.abstract:
In this paper, we obtain a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > B_ex for every finite-order Hecke L-function over every number field, where B_ex = 0.87407284766682790777... is an explicitly defined algebraic number of degree four. The proof refines the cubic-theta comparison in two parts. In Part I, we require sufficient prime-product length for length restoration and fix the short side of the equal-product comparison rectangle at 1/4. Direct and complementary Poisson estimates give an amplified Gauss norm with an additional prime product. Its separate applications to the numerator and the counting detector, combined with contour displacement and successive moment bounds, give the intermediate boundary B′ = 0.87422125049290208328....

In Part II, complete prime removal is permitted even when a positive length excess remains. The no-prime moment estimate then controls the resulting ordinary sums, and the comparison rectangle’s short side may vary. These changes remove the coupled condition on the remaining prime length and enlarge the allowed norm widths. The improved detector count and numerator estimate give successive proved bounds converging to B_ex. We prove optimality for this specified direct, detector and fourth-moment comparison system, retaining its geometric length inequality while allowing the sum of the length exponents to vary. Both parts use the established theta, moment and continuation results of the earlier QRH papers and their general-field formulation.

candidates.title: Closed three-manifolds as hypersurfaces of Euclidean fourspace: compactness, the homogeneous geometries, and total absolute curvature
candidates.abstract:
## Abstract

Let $(\Sigma, g)$ be a closed Riemannian three-manifold, and let $\mathbb M = -G$ be its negative Einstein endomorphism.
Where $\det\mathbb M > 0$, the companion paper [MA] reduces realizability as a hypersurface of $E^4$ to one equation,
$F(g) = 0$, and studies it locally. Here we treat the global questions.

- **Compactness.** A closed realization has $\det\mathbb M \geq R^{-6}$ at a point farthest from any centre, where $R$ is that
  distance, and so $\max\det\mathbb M \geq 125/(8\,\mathrm{diam}^6)$ by Jung's theorem. If $\det\mathbb M > 0$ everywhere, the realization is a strictly
  convex embedded sphere, unique up to rigid motion. So a closed connected metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ is realizable iff
  $\Sigma$ is simply connected and $F(g) = 0$. No closed three-manifold other than $S^3$ carries such a realizable metric.
- **The homogeneous geometries.** A realizable closed metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ and constant scalar curvature is round,
  and so is every compact locally homogeneous realization. Locally, constant $\mathbb M$-eigenvalues with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ force
  constant curvature, a case of Tsukada's classification. This recovers Agaoka and Hashinaga's list of the
  left-invariant metrics that embed locally. The eight Thurston geometries are worked as checks.
- **Total absolute curvature.** $J(g) = \int\sqrt{\det\mathbb M}\,dV$ equals $2\pi^2$ on every closed realizable metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$, so
  any other value excludes realizability. At the round sphere $J$ is stationary. Its second variation on
  transverse-traceless tensors of level $n$ is $-(\mu_n + 2)(\mu_n + 3)/16$ times the squared norm, $\mu_n = n^2 - 3$, and its
  radical is exactly the conformal and Lie directions. On conformal rays $J$ is flat to third order. Along the
  conformal path of [MA], $J = 2\pi^2 - \pi^2t^4/12 + O(t^6)$.
- **Non-convex realizations.** Embedded hypersurfaces of revolution are non-convex exactly around their necks. For
  the radial graphs $r = 1 + \varepsilon\cos2\chi$, convexity is lost at $\varepsilon = 1/5$ in a Whitney cusp of the Gauss map. With
  $\delta = \varepsilon - 1/5$, the relative excess $J/2\pi^2 - 1$ then grows as $500\,\delta^{3/2}/(9\sqrt2\,\pi)$.
- **Connectivity, and the round sphere.** Modulo isometry, the closed realizable metrics with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ form a
  contractible family, contracted by an explicit equivariant path. The embedded hypersurfaces of revolution join
  the round sphere through the degenerate locus. We collect the characterisations of the round sphere, with their
  hypotheses.

Every displayed result is reproduced by a script; Appendix V indexes them.

candidates.title: Riemannian three-manifolds as hypersurfaces of Euclidean four-space: the realizability operator, its symbol, and its linearisation at the round sphere
candidates.abstract: For a Riemannian three-manifold $(\Sigma,g)$ with negative Einstein endomorphism $\mathbb{M}=-G$, the Gauss equation of a hypersurface of $\mathbb{R}^4$ reads $\mathbb{M}=\mathrm{adj}\,K$, and on $\{\det\mathbb{M}>0\}$ it is solved identically by $\tilde K=\sqrt{\det\mathbb{M}}\,\mathbb{M}^{-1}$. Realizability with nondegenerate second fundamental form is therefore the single equation $F(g)=\mathrm{Cod}(\tilde K(g))=0$. The reduction is classical (Beez, Killing, Thomas) and the zero set has been characterized intrinsically (Rivertz; Agaoka and Hashinaga); we study $F$ as a nonlinear operator on metrics. At every nondegenerate point its principal symbol has rank two, with kernel exactly the symbol of the linearised immersions, so $F$ is injective modulo immersions everywhere and nowhere elliptic modulo diffeomorphisms alone. The nine Codazzi components carry four identities, leaving five conditions at every nondegenerate point, and Cartan's test holds with equality, in exact arithmetic, off a proper real-algebraic set. On a closed manifold the zero set is nowhere dense in the nondegenerate domain. At the round $S^3$ the linearisation on transverse-traceless tensors is $\mathrm{Cod}\circ\frac{1}{2}(-\Delta+2)$, with singular values $n(n^2-1)/\sqrt{2}$ and $\|DF\,h\|^2\ge 288\|h\|^2$. For metrics foliated by round 2-spheres we solve the first-order problem in closed form and write down all hypersurfaces swept by round 2-spheres; the $\ell=1$ direction is realized exactly by tilting the spheres' 3-planes. We treat the degenerate locus by two polynomial forms, and give Gauss–Codazzi as the flatness of two $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connections: on the nondegenerate domain, realizability is equivalent to a single parallel spinor. Every displayed result is checked by a deposited script.
