candidates.abstract: Kernel-checked proof, for every Coxeter system on three generators a, b, c with m(a,c) = p, m(b,c) = q, m(a,b) = infinity and p, q >= 2, of the growth-series identity in the ring of integer power series: (sum_n a(n) X^n) * (1 - (X + ... + X^(p-1))(X + ... + X^(q-1))) = (1 + X)(1 + ... + X^(p-1))(1 + ... + X^(q-1)), where a(n) is the number of group elements of Coxeter length n; together with its instances (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf), (3,3,inf) and, for (2,3,inf) = PGL(2,Z), the sphere sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, ..., the Padovan identity a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, the two-sided bounds 2 rho^n <= a(n) <= 4 rho^n (n >= 2), and the growth rate a(n)^(1/n) -> rho, the plastic number, the unique real root > 1 of x^3 = x + 1; and, for the whole family, monotonicity and symmetry in (p, q), the growth rate of every hyperbolic member, and the minimality of the plastic number. Twenty compared theorems: (1) the general identity for all p, q >= 2; (2) non-vacuity, a Coxeter matrix of that type exists for all p, q >= 2; (3)-(5) the three instances; (6) the (2,3,inf) sphere sizes a(0..4) = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and the recursion a(n+5) = a(n+3) + a(n+2) for all n; (7) that the recursion fails one step earlier, a(4) != a(2) + a(1); (8) a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, for any sequence with the Padovan initial values and recursion; (9) existence and uniqueness of the plastic number; (10) the bounds; (11) the n-th-root limit; (12) monotonicity: a(n) of a (p,q,inf) system is at most a(n) of a (p',q',inf) system for p <= p', q <= q'; (13) symmetry in p and q; (14) 2 rho^n <= a(n), n >= 2, for every hyperbolic member; (15) for (p,q) != (2,2) exactly one tau > 1 solves (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1))(tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1; (16) a(n)^(1/n) -> tau; (17) tau strictly increasing in (p,q); (18) rho <= tau with equality exactly at (2,3), (3,2), so the plastic number is the minimal growth rate of the family; (19) tau < 2; (20) tau -> 2 as p, q -> infinity (for every sigma < 2 there is N with tau > sigma whenever p, q >= N). The family statements (12)-(20) give the growth rate of every hyperbolic (p, q, inf) group as the unique root tau > 1 of an explicit equation, strictly increasing in the labels, with the plastic number as the family minimum attained only at (2,3,inf) and (3,2,inf); they restrict to this family, and kernel-check there, Terragni's monotonicity (2016, Thm. A), Floyd's planar minimality (1992, p. 482) and the continuity of the growth rate (Floyd 1992; Yukita 2024). The mathematics is classical and no novelty is claimed for it: the growth series of a Coxeter group is rational and determined by its finite parabolic subgroups (Steinberg 1968; Humphreys 1990 Section 5.12); growth of planar hyperbolic Coxeter groups is Floyd 1992 and Cannon-Wagreich 1992, and the (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf) and (3,3,inf) sphere sequences are OEIS A096231, A179070 (shifted) and A054886, with generating functions derived there from Cannon-Wagreich Prop. 3.1 and, for A096231, the Padovan form a(n) = A000931(n+10) recorded; Floyd 1992 (p. 482) proves (2,3,inf) minimal among cusped planar groups and Kellerhals 2013 gives an alternative proof; Bucher-Talambutsa 2016 Prop. 18 proves statement (11) itself by a normal form and, with Mann's bound, the minimality of rho for PGL(2,Z) over all generating sets. The (p, q, inf) family is hyperbolic exactly when (p, q) differs from (2, 2); the affine (2, 2, inf) is included in (1). The contribution claimed is the kernel-checked general identity for all p, q at once, and the family statements (12)-(20) derived from it, from Mathlib's CoxeterSystem alone — Mathlib at this pin has no growth series, no exchange or deletion property and no parabolic-subgroup API — by constructing the amalgam normal forms, lifting their action to the group, proving Coxeter length equals normal-form length, and counting. No "first formalization" claim is made. Application, cited and not a claim of the entry: the (2,3,inf) group is the Weyl group of AE_3 = PGL(2,Z) (Feingold-Frenkel 1983) and, in the Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai billiard description of the Belinski-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz limit (a conjecture for generic singularities, Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 2.9), the reflection group of the billiard of 3+1-dimensional vacuum gravity near a spacelike singularity (Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai 2003 Section 8; Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 3.1), where a(n) counts the chambers reachable from the fundamental chamber after exactly n wall collisions over all initial data, so (10)-(11) give the growth rate of those outcomes (elementary reflection-group geometry, not formal content). Hypotheses are inline: the Coxeter system enters through Mathlib's CoxeterSystem with the three matrix entries as hypotheses, rho through its defining equation and 1 < rho, the Padovan sequence through its initial values and recursion; the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (CoxeterMatrix, CoxeterSystem, CoxeterSystem.length, Nat.card, PowerSeries.mk, Finset.range/Ico sums, Filter.Tendsto, Filter.atTop, nhds, real powers) — zero custom definitions. The pinned source of each Coxeter-specific imported definition, and of Nat.card and PowerSeries.mk, is quoted verbatim, with permalinks, in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md (the remaining vocabulary is standard Mathlib and is not quoted), and DefinitionAudit.lean kernel-checks the facts the statements rely on (the entry 0 encodes infinity; length is the minimal word length; spheres are finite and Nat.card is their cardinality; every Coxeter matrix has a Coxeter system).

candidates.title: Resonance-cluster analysis for a proposed counterexample to Fried's conjecture
candidates.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of the theorem FriedCrossing.fried_counterexample_of_resolvent_inputs, the machine-checked reduction behind a proposed codimension-one failure of Fried's identity ζ(0) = τ_R for acyclic characters on a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with b₁ = 1. For a simple illustration of the method with figures, see docs/counterexample_intuitive_view.pdf.
The Mechanism: Near (g_hyp, ρ_triv), along the conformal family g_τ = e^{−2τb}g_hyp with characters χ_θ, the Ruelle resonances near 0 form two small clusters: a rank-2 cluster in degree 1, encoded by a 2×2 matrix M(θ,τ), and a rank-4 cluster in degree 2, encoded by a 4×4 matrix A(θ,τ). A branch is one eigenvalue of a cluster matrix followed continuously in (θ,τ). Degree 1 has the closed branch and the twin s_nc(θ,τ), which starts at the double point s*(θ) < 0 and travels at rate r₀ > 0 towards 0. Degree 2 has the two locked branches (the same eigenvalues, lifted by d₀) and two pure branches, the roots of Q = X² − e₁X + e₂; the pure branch nearest 0 is z(θ,τ). At the crossing metric τ = σ(θ) the twin and z reach 0 together, the twin as a pole of ζ and z as a zero, so ζ stays regular at 0 and ζ(0; g_σ) = τ_R · (rate of the twin)/(rate of z). The twin's rate is at most 2r₀ and z's exceeds 2r₀, so ζ(0; g_σ) ≠ τ_R. Fried's identity would need the two branches to arrive at the same speed. The whole Lean argument is bookkeeping of these four branches.
What is Proved: The theorem is a conditional reduction. Its objects are two abstract resolvent families on Banach scales (structure fields = the cited facts: local uniform boundedness and two-sided inversion of the generator modulo inclusions, CDDP Lemma 4.3; smooth generator), complex structures, and nondegenerate frames; the cluster matrices M, A are DEFINED from them as real parts of the frame matrices A(p)⁻¹B(p) built from contour integrals of matrix elements of the resolvent. Its hypotheses are, in six groups, the properties of that data which the argument uses, each cited: (1) two independent states at s*(θ) in the degree-1 cluster at τ = 0, with s*(0) = 0, s* continuous, s*(θ) < 0 for θ ≠ 0 [DGRS (7.6), BuOl Cor 5.1, DFG Thm 2; independence = rederivation A2 of the informal account]; (2) the first-variation formula B·∂_τM(0,0) = diag(0,p) with r₀ = B_cc p/det B > 0 [CDDP (4.22), (1.3)]; (3) the degree-2 cluster at τ = 0 has spectrum {s*, s*, s*, −s*} [DGRS (7.6), k = 2]; (4) at θ = 0 the degree-1 cluster is singular and the degree-2 cluster has spectrum {0, 0, 0, tr M} [CDDP Cor 4.1, DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (5) every eigenvalue of M is an eigenvalue of A [DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (6) for any functions ζ₀, F, any τ_R ≠ 0 and dimension vector c: ζ₀ = F·z/s_nc off the crossing with F continuous and ζ₀(σ) = F(σ) at it [CD (6.5) at λ = 0], ζ₀ = τ_R wherever s_nc ≠ 0 [DGRS Thm 2 + Fried 1986], exactness of C₀¹ → C₀² → V₃ at each crossing [DR Thm 2.1], c₀ = c₄ = 0 and c₃ = c₁ [DGRS Lemmas 7.4, 7.2], c_k the dimensions. The conclusion: there are θ₀, δ > 0 such that for 0 < |θ| < θ₀ the twin crosses 0 at exactly one σ ∈ (0, 2|s*|/r₀], the ζ-order at 0 is zero, the zero branch has slope ∂_τe₂/e₁ of modulus > 2r₀, |e₁(θ,σ)| ≤ K₁|θ|σ, and ζ₀(σ) = τ_R · (pole rate)/(zero rate) ≠ τ_R, with the torsion identity of the zero cluster.
Dependencies: The identification of the abstract data with the geometry — that the resolvent families are those of the twisted deformed generator L_X + iθω(X) on the anisotropic spaces of g_τ, that ζ₀(τ) is the Ruelle zeta function of g_τ at 0, that τ_R is the Reidemeister torsion of χ_θ, and that the defined matrices are the cluster matrices (their imaginary parts vanish) — is the informal layer, taken from the cited papers and the accompanying note, and is not formalized. Nothing about manifolds, flows, anisotropic spaces or zeta functions is in Lean. Granting the six groups as cited, the theorem exhibits a counterexample to Fried's identity in the form stated by DGRS for acyclic unitary representations, at a non-generic metric where ζ is regular at 0 and zero-resonant states exist with cancelling multiplicities; the refined identity of CD Thm 4 holds there. Whether the six groups hold as cited has not been independently verified by a mathematician other than the author.

routes.title: Are canonical tangent cones of proper lower-curvature spaces separable?

candidates.title: A Counterexample to the Trace Problem for Uniform Tracial Completions
candidates.abstract: We formalize a negative answer to Problem XXII of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White. There is a separable unital C*-algebra A with nonempty compact tracial state space such that its uniform tracial completion M has a tracial state that is discontinuous in the uniform 2-norm. Thus the canonical extensions of the traces of A form a proper subset X of the traces of M. A second theorem gives a factorial tracially complete pair (M, X) with the same failure, answering Question 1.1 of Carrion, Castillejos, Evington, Gabe, Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White negatively. In both statements, X is exactly the set of uniform-2-norm-continuous traces. The proof uses a unitized c0-sum of antipodally covariant matrix-function algebras of growing rank and dimension. Borsuk-Ulam supplies finite coordinate-state constraints; weak-star compactness produces a corona trace detecting a sequence whose uniform 2-norm tends to zero. Both selected Lean theorems are unconditional. The completion is characterized by tracial completeness, unique restriction of designated traces to all base traces, and density in the uniform 2-norm.

routes.title: The strong maximal-rank conjecture for linear series on a general curve

candidates.title: Natural Cohomology of General Steiner Bundles
candidates.abstract:
We prove that a general Steiner bundle on projective space over a field of characteris-
tic zero has natural cohomology. The proof constructs a matrix of linear forms from multiplication
of sections on a curve. When the rank exceeds the dimension of the projective space, a finite étale
isogeny of elliptic curves splits the bundles controlling the graded kernels and cokernels into line
bundles of equal degree. Choosing the auxiliary line bundle outside a finite set gives maximal
rank in every degree. A rational curve provides the boundary case. Two open rank conditions
then yield the assertion for general matrices and all twists.

candidates.title: Natural cohomology of general Steiner bundles
candidates.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Natural Cohomology of General Steiner Bundles. Over every characteristic-zero field, for all n >= 1, t >= 1, and r >= n, a nonempty principal open of t by (t+r) matrices of linear forms on projective n-space has maximal rank in every homogeneous degree. The transposes give exact Steiner presentations of actual rank-r locally free sheaves, whose integer twists each have at most one nonzero sheaf cohomology group. The coefficient open is nonempty over the original field.

routes.title: What is the optimal power exponent for the four-corner Favard length?

candidates.title: The Favard-length decay exponent of the four-corner Cantor set is at least 1/4
candidates.abstract: For the four-corner Cantor set approximants K_n = C_n × C_n, where C_n is the union of the 2^n intervals of length 4^{-n} with left endpoints sum_{j<=n} w_j 4^{-j}, w_j in {0,3}, let α_Fav be the supremum of the a >= 0 for which the Favard length Fav(K_n) = (1/π) ∫_0^π |π_θ(K_n)| dθ is at most C n^{-a} for all n >= 1. This project proves in Lean that every a < 1/4 is admissible, so 1/4 <= α_Fav, together with the classical bound α_Fav <= 1. The previous best lower bounds were 1/6 (Nazarov-Peres-Volberg, 2010) and 1/5 (Marshall, arXiv:2509.02882 v2, 2026, whose v1 claim of 1/4 was withdrawn). The new ingredient is a joint negative-moment estimate for the low-frequency cosine product. The argument comes from an unpublished AI-assisted manuscript, and this formalization is its first complete proof.

routes.title: Minimum-volume convex bodies of prescribed minimum width

candidates.title: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
candidates.abstract:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. The proof writes |G| - Q as a sum of nonnegative terms, and the energy terms among them also bound that distance. The bound is attained: Gerver's triple lies in the enlarged domain, and Q equals |G| there.

From the certificate: optimality, Baek's theorem, proved without his Theorem 1.1.1 and without the balance argument of his Chapters 4 to 6; uniqueness, every moving sofa with the area of G is mapped onto G by a rotation and a translation (a translation suffices); and stability, after a translation a moving sofa of area |G| - epsilon lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance C sqrt(epsilon) of G, their symmetric difference has area at most C' sqrt(epsilon), its rotation angle misses a right angle by at most C'' epsilon, and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved. The Challenge also states the correspondence between Baek's definitions and those of Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and formal-conjectures' statements, among them the uniqueness, which it lists as open; here they are proved through the certificate.

Versions 1 to 4 of this entry registered the formalization of Baek's paper with a first proof of uniqueness that uses his Theorem 1.1.1; they state the same optimality, uniqueness and formal-conjectures theorems, proved through Baek's argument, and the repository keeps their Challenge and Solution in baek/. This version proves those theorems through the certificate and adds the certificate and the stability. A script in the repository, scripts/AuditCoerciveRoute.lean, run by the continuous integration, checks that its proofs reach neither Baek's Theorem 1.1.1, nor the results of his balance argument, nor the main theorem and the equality analysis of the first proof of uniqueness.

candidates.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorems A and B of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. For every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic order of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex central configuration with that cyclic order, up to similarity, so there are exactly three convex central configurations up to similarity. This answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos (2012). The main step of the paper is Theorem B: at every strictly convex central configuration of positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least one quarter of its radial part K. It follows that every convex central configuration is a nondegenerate local minimum of U I^(1/2), whose Hessian vanishes exactly on the tangent space of the orbit of the similarities. The computer-assisted step, a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations in the coordinates of Corbera, Cors and Roberts, proves tr S < 3/4 and is checked by Lean's kernel with `decide +kernel` in 7307 certificate theorems. No compiled code is trusted, and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

routes.title: Smooth classification of four-manifolds with conformal curvature ratio below eight

candidates.title: Closed three-manifolds as hypersurfaces of Euclidean fourspace: compactness, the homogeneous geometries, and total absolute curvature
candidates.abstract:
## Abstract

Let $(\Sigma, g)$ be a closed Riemannian three-manifold, and let $\mathbb M = -G$ be its negative Einstein endomorphism.
Where $\det\mathbb M > 0$, the companion paper [MA] reduces realizability as a hypersurface of $E^4$ to one equation,
$F(g) = 0$, and studies it locally. Here we treat the global questions.

- **Compactness.** A closed realization has $\det\mathbb M \geq R^{-6}$ at a point farthest from any centre, where $R$ is that
  distance, and so $\max\det\mathbb M \geq 125/(8\,\mathrm{diam}^6)$ by Jung's theorem. If $\det\mathbb M > 0$ everywhere, the realization is a strictly
  convex embedded sphere, unique up to rigid motion. So a closed connected metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ is realizable iff
  $\Sigma$ is simply connected and $F(g) = 0$. No closed three-manifold other than $S^3$ carries such a realizable metric.
- **The homogeneous geometries.** A realizable closed metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ and constant scalar curvature is round,
  and so is every compact locally homogeneous realization. Locally, constant $\mathbb M$-eigenvalues with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ force
  constant curvature, a case of Tsukada's classification. This recovers Agaoka and Hashinaga's list of the
  left-invariant metrics that embed locally. The eight Thurston geometries are worked as checks.
- **Total absolute curvature.** $J(g) = \int\sqrt{\det\mathbb M}\,dV$ equals $2\pi^2$ on every closed realizable metric with $\det\mathbb M > 0$, so
  any other value excludes realizability. At the round sphere $J$ is stationary. Its second variation on
  transverse-traceless tensors of level $n$ is $-(\mu_n + 2)(\mu_n + 3)/16$ times the squared norm, $\mu_n = n^2 - 3$, and its
  radical is exactly the conformal and Lie directions. On conformal rays $J$ is flat to third order. Along the
  conformal path of [MA], $J = 2\pi^2 - \pi^2t^4/12 + O(t^6)$.
- **Non-convex realizations.** Embedded hypersurfaces of revolution are non-convex exactly around their necks. For
  the radial graphs $r = 1 + \varepsilon\cos2\chi$, convexity is lost at $\varepsilon = 1/5$ in a Whitney cusp of the Gauss map. With
  $\delta = \varepsilon - 1/5$, the relative excess $J/2\pi^2 - 1$ then grows as $500\,\delta^{3/2}/(9\sqrt2\,\pi)$.
- **Connectivity, and the round sphere.** Modulo isometry, the closed realizable metrics with $\det\mathbb M > 0$ form a
  contractible family, contracted by an explicit equivariant path. The embedded hypersurfaces of revolution join
  the round sphere through the degenerate locus. We collect the characterisations of the round sphere, with their
  hypotheses.

Every displayed result is reproduced by a script; Appendix V indexes them.

candidates.title: Systolic growth in every genus
candidates.abstract: This repository introduces and formally proves the lower bound 4/3 for the limit inferior of the supremal hyperbolic systole in genus g divided by log g. At present, this formalization is the theorem's only public statement and proof. This metadata records the result as an original proof; the published papers below are cited only as background for ingredients. The proof combines arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, uniform representations by comparable prime cubes, and surface gluing followed by a smooth conformal change to curvature minus one that preserves the systole lower bound.

routes.title: Do nearest-point strata of finitely many convex sites have finitely many components?

candidates.title: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values
candidates.abstract: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.

candidates.title: Linnik's constant is at most 3.99: A formalization of a weighted version of Heath-Brown's near-density estimate, and of the proof's certificate checker
candidates.abstract: Two components of the proof, in the paper "Linnik's constant is at most 3.99" (paper/linnik399.pdf in this repository), that every reduced residue class modulo q contains a prime below q^3.99 for all large q. That bound itself is NOT formally verified here: the paper's zero-location arguments, case analysis and exterior regimes have conventional proofs and computer checks only. (1) The graded near lemma: fix test data (a detector f satisfying Heath-Brown's Condition 1, a Gram test g satisfying his Conditions 1 and 2, a Selberg-sieve weight with heights h_k >= 0 on cells [t_k, t_{k+1}) with t_0 > 1/3 + 2 eps', finitely many nonnegative anchor offsets, a positive lower bound for the weight omega where f is nonzero, and I_B > 0) and eta > 0. For all large q, take a finite family of entries (chi_j, gamma_j, delta_j) of non-principal characters mod q with heights |gamma_j| <= T <= (log q)/3 and a safe anchor at height 2T+1, whose characters are pairwise distinct whenever some sieve height h_k is nonzero (condition (iii) of the paper's Theorem 8.4; without sieve weights a character may repeat, and repeated characters enter through the pair excess e_j). Then the prime-sum responses satisfy (sum_j a_j R_j)_+^2 <= (1+eta) I_B [sum_j (D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j) a_j^2 + (d_1 + eta)(sum_j a_j)^2] for all a_j >= 0. This is a weighted version of Heath-Brown's Lemma 12.1 (1992), which Heath-Brown remarks (section 16, item 9) no neat way of achieving "seems available". Its zero form: the response lemma (a response is bounded below by the zeros it keeps, via the local explicit formula), the threshold form exists tau: sum_j (v_j - tau)_+^2 / D_j <= 1 - tau^2/d with features computed from kept zeros, provided every diagonal numerator D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j is positive, the entry bounds F(hi - s_j) of the rows, the normalization used by the leaf builders, and the vanishing of the pair excess for separated same-character pairs. (2) The leaf LPs: an exact integer checker for the certificates of the leaf linear programs (bisection trees over threshold boxes, first-order and tangent relaxations with safe rounding, exclusions, weak duality with a free dual) is proved sound: if it accepts a certificate with value v, every feasible point of the LP has objective at most v < 10^16. A bridge lemma turns the threshold form into the LP's near rows. Seven certificates (six leaves of the 3.99 corpus and the program of the large first-zero range) are checked by the kernel (decide +kernel) in the repository (not part of the compared theorems). The analytic part is conditional on four published estimates, stated as explicit hypotheses in the Challenge, each no stronger than its source: Xylouris's Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 (= Heath-Brown's Lemmas 5.3 and 5.2), Burgess's character-sum bound with k = 3 as printed for primitive characters (Heath-Brown's Lemma 2.1; the form for all non-principal characters is derived), and Graham's asymptotic for Selberg-sieve sums. Mertens' estimate, Abel and partial summation, the Selberg majorant, the decay of Laplace transforms, the finiteness and multiplicities of zeros in a disc, the equality of multiplicities of conjugate zeros for real characters, and all error bookkeeping are proved.

routes.title: Rational coefficients in supernatural decompositions of sheaf cohomology

candidates.title: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds and the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Markman)
candidates.abstract:
A conditional Lean 4 formalization of E. Markman, "Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds" (arXiv:2502.03415v2). The paper proves that the Hodge-Weil classes of polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 are algebraic (Theorem 1.5.1) and deduces the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.6.1).

Every result of the paper about cohomology classes, Clifford algebras, spin representations, Hodge structures and period domains is proved in a linear-algebra model of the cohomology of abelian varieties (abelian varieties up to isogeny as polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight one), by the paper's arguments except the departures listed under fidelity (notably Proposition 6.1.2 and Lemma 4.0.2, proved by other arguments with the owner's approval): rational secant lines to the spinor variety and the abelian 2n-folds of Weil type they give (Sections 2-4), the Spin(V)-equivariance of Orlov's equivalence (Section 6, Proposition 6.1.2), Theorem 1.4.1(3) and (4) (the characteristic class of the secant-square sheaf stays of Hodge type on every Weil-type deformation of X x X^, and its K-translates with h^3 span Q h^3 + HW), Corollary 1.3.2, the cohomological results of Section 8, and Section 10. The results the paper cites from Chevalley, Igusa (Lemmas 1-2, Section 2, Proposition 3 except the orbits over subfields in which -d is not a square), Golyshev-Lunts-Orlov, Orlov, Huybrechts, Trautman, van Geemen (Def. 4.9, and Th. 5.2(3) through Landherr's theorem and Meyer's theorem), Markman (2023) and Schoen (Prop. 10, from push-forward of cycles, by Voisin's argument) are proved in the case the paper uses.

Theorem 1.5.1 and Corollary 1.6.1 are proved assuming, as named hypotheses in their statements, the paper's own sheaf-theoretic Sections 7-9 (in the form: the class kappa_3(E) is algebraic near X x X^ wherever kappa(E) is of Hodge type) and results from algebraic geometry not yet available in Lean: about algebraic cycles, pullbacks, push-forwards along projections and products of algebraic classes, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Voisin's algebraicity loci and a theorem of Ramon-Mari; about Hodge structures, two theorems of Moonen-Zarhin. Remark 10.1.2(1) assumes part of Igusa's Proposition 3 when -d is not a square. Eleven statements of the paper are false or misprinted as printed and are formalized in corrected form (the basis of Example 10.2.2 is also misprinted, with no effect on the value computed there); REPORT.md audits the paper.

routes.title: One homothety factor for optimal convex-body covers in every dimension

candidates.title: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

candidates.title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines: 2 − 1/m, 4/3 − 1/(3m) and their tight instances
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Graham's two bounds for scheduling independent jobs on identical machines to minimize the makespan (R. L. Graham, Bounds for certain multiprocessing anomalies, Bell System Tech. J. 45 (1966) 1563-1581; Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 17 (1969) 416-429; both restated with their examples in his survey Bounds on multiprocessing anomalies and related packing algorithms, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference (1972) 205-217). n jobs of nonnegative real lengths p : Fin n -> R are run without interruption on m >= 1 identical machines; an assignment sigma : Fin n -> Fin m loads machine i with the sum of the lengths assigned to it, its makespan is the largest load, and optMakespan m p is the least makespan over all m^n assignments. A list schedule (IsListSchedule, in the index order) gives each job a machine whose load from the earlier jobs is least, under any tie-breaking (a relation, so every theorem covers every tie-breaking); an LPT schedule (IsLPTSchedule) is a list schedule of the jobs in some nonincreasing order of length. Theorems, kernel-only: every list schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy m * C(sigma) <= (2m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1966, his Theorem for the same number of processors and no precedence constraints), so C(sigma) <= (2 - 1/m) * optMakespan; the m(m - 1) unit jobs followed by one job of length m (Graham's example for his theorem on scheduling the k largest tasks optimally first, at k = 0, as his 1972 survey restates it; Lenstra-Shmoys, Chapter 9, p. 188) have optimum m and every list schedule of them in that order has makespan 2m - 1, so 2 - 1/m is the least constant (IsLeast); every LPT schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy 3m * C(sigma) <= (4m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1969, Theorem 2, announced in the closing remarks of the 1966 paper), so C(sigma) <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) * optMakespan; when every job is longer than a third of C(tau), every LPT schedule is at least as good as tau, so LPT is optimal when every job exceeds a third of the optimum; Graham's 2m + 1 jobs 2m - 1, 2m - 1, 2m - 2, 2m - 2, ..., m + 1, m + 1, m, m, m (his pp. 425-426) are in nonincreasing order, have optimum 3m, attained by a list schedule in the order 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m, m, 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m (the definition grahamOrder, a permutation of the jobs whose lengths are that list), and every LPT schedule of them has makespan 4m - 1, for every m >= 1, so 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least constant (IsLeast); and the elementary facts (list and LPT schedules exist, the optimum is attained, every load, every job and the average load are at most the makespan, relabeling the jobs preserves the makespan); Graham's omega_0, the least finishing time over all lists, equals the optimum over all assignments (every assignment is matched or improved by a list schedule in some order), so the bounds against every assignment are his; for his instance the optimum is attained by an explicit list (grahamOrder); and the third of the optimality theorem cannot be weakened (on three machines 9, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, each job at least a third of the optimum 12, has an LPT schedule of makespan 13, so n <= 2m jobs do not make LPT optimal; Graham's 1972 survey prints Spencer's 6, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 for the same purpose); and the position of a job on its machine: the (c + 1)-th job k placed on a machine of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p has (c + 1) p_k <= C(tau) for every assignment tau (the property of Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia 2020 restate it; proved here by an invariant on pairs of machines), hence the Coffman-Sethi form q m C(sigma) <= ((q + 1) m - 1) C(tau) for a machine with q jobs attaining the makespan of an LPT schedule (Coffman-Sethi 1976 as corrected by Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia restate it; the literature states it for q >= 3, for m >= 2 it is weaker than the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound at q <= 2, and neither its attainment nor Chen's 4/3 - 1/(3(m - 1)) at q = 2 is proved here; Chen's and Coffman-Sethi's papers were not read). The proof of the LPT bound is by counting, not by his exchange argument: with k the job ending a heaviest machine, the average-load bound settles 3 p_k <= C(tau), and otherwise a count of the jobs up to k (every machine of tau holds at most two of them, those at least as long as the least load sit alone, each single-job machine of sigma contributes one) shows that k's machine ends by C(tau). Further: for a job k completing at the makespan of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p, the smaller of C(sigma) and 3 p_k is at most C(tau) for every tau, and C(sigma) <= 3 p_k certifies optimality; equality 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) C(tau) on m >= 2 machines forces 3 p_k = C(tau), equal loads before k, every load of tau equal to C(tau) and no positive job after k; Della Croce-Scatamacchia's Proposition 4, q (m - 1) C(sigma) <= ((q + 1)(m - 1) - 1) C(tau) when another machine holds q jobs before k and q + 2 <= m, proved from Chen's property; Dósa's theorem (2004, Theorem 2: Graham's example is the only tight one): every positive multiple of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs in any order attains the bound, and for a nonempty positive instance on m >= 2 machines a list schedule in nonincreasing order, or an LPT schedule in any order, attains 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) optMakespan only when the instance is a positive multiple of Graham's jobs, so the inequality is strict for every number of jobs other than 2m + 1; and for every fixed n >= 2m + 1 the constant 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the supremum (IsLUB) of C(sigma)/optMakespan over the LPT schedules of the positive instances with n jobs (the proof approaches it with Graham's jobs followed by small jobs; Dósa's Remark 1 asserts a strict gap for every n != 2m + 1, which can therefore hold at most for n < 2m + 1, not formalized here). Forty-one compared statements over nine fully specified definitions; the finite facts behind every statement are replayed exactly in the standard library by scripts/check_lpt.py. As of 2026-10-11 no kernel-checked proof of the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound, of either equality family or of the optimality statement was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, anthropics/formal-math, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index, GitHub code search in Lean or arXiv; the AFP's Approximation_Algorithms proves a 3/2 bound for sorted greedy and the factor 2 for greedy, and two Lean repositories prove m * C <= sum p + (m - 1) * p_max over lists of naturals. No priority is claimed.

candidates.title: Systolic growth in every genus
candidates.abstract: This repository introduces and formally proves the lower bound 4/3 for the limit inferior of the supremal hyperbolic systole in genus g divided by log g. At present, this formalization is the theorem's only public statement and proof. This metadata records the result as an original proof; the published papers below are cited only as background for ingredients. The proof combines arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, uniform representations by comparable prime cubes, and surface gluing followed by a smooth conformal change to curvature minus one that preserves the systole lower bound.

candidates.title: The augmented Descartes theorem in every dimension, its converses, and Soddy's two spheres
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Section 3 of Lagarias, Mallows and Wilks, Beyond the Descartes circle theorem (Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 338-361), in the Lorentz form. An oriented sphere in R^n with centre x and signed radius r has the augmented curvature-centre row (|x|^2/r - r, 1/r, x/r); an oriented hyperplane <h, y> = delta with unit normal h has the row (2 delta, 0, h) (LMW Definition 3.2, (3.7)-(3.9)). Tangency is distance-encoded in LMW's oriented sense: two spheres dist^2 = (r + s)^2 (external tangency for two positive radii, internal when one radius is negative), a sphere and a hyperplane <h, x> - delta = -r, two hyperplanes opposite unit normals, LMW's oriented tangency pair by pair, and the converses deliver tangency in this sense; the compatible orientations of an oriented Descartes configuration (disjoint interiors, with the given orientations or all reversed) are proved separately for every solution, after multiplying each row's power polynomial by the total curvature, and for a valid, pairwise tangent family with positive total curvature for its own open interiors. Kernel-checked, for every n >= 1 (LMW's Section 3 assumes n >= 2; their Section 8, (8.4), is the identity on the line): the augmented matrix W of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres of nonzero curvature, and of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres and hyperplanes, satisfies W^T Q_n W = [[0, -4, 0], [-4, 0, 0], [0, 0, 2 I_n]] with Q_n = I - (1/n) 11^T (Theorem 3.3); every real solution W is the augmented matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes, and, when its second column has no zero, of exactly one pairwise tangent family of spheres (the converse of Theorem 3.3); the Soddy-Gosset relation (sum 1/r_i)^2 = n sum (1/r_i)^2 with and without hyperplanes (Theorem 1.2, (1.2)) and its form b^T Q_n b = 0 ((3.2)); the curvature-centre identity M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) (Theorem 3.2, (3.5)); at n = 2 the complex Descartes theorem (sum b_i z_i)^2 = 2 sum (b_i z_i)^2 and sum b_i (b_i z_i) = (1/2)(sum b_i)(sum b_i z_i) (Theorem 2.1, (2.2)-(2.3)); det Q_n = -2/n; and the three statements for Mathlib's EuclideanGeometry.Sphere (pairwise IsExtTangent, or one enclosing sphere to which the others are IsIntTangent, with curvature -1/r_e). The matrix identity is proved as LMW's Section 4 argument (Lemmas 4.3-4.4, (4.9)-(4.10)) run directly in Euclidean coordinates: W^T Q_n W is the target exactly when the rows of W have Lorentz norm 1 and pair to -1 under G = [[0, -1/2, 0], [-1/2, 0, 0], [0, 0, I_n]], since W G W^T = 2I - J and (2I - J)(Q_n/2) = I. Also proved: both halves of the converse of the Soddy-Gosset theorem, LMW's Theorem 3.1, about which they write "We do not know an easy proof of this result; a proof appears in [16]" ([16] is Graham-Lagarias-Mallows-Wilks-Yan III, whose arXiv versions 1-2 prove both halves as their Theorem 2.2 from the same base configuration and the transitivity of the Lorentz group, a section the published version omits). Existence: every nonzero b with (sum b_i)^2 = n sum b_i^2 is the curvature vector of a pairwise tangent family of spheres, where b_i is nonzero, and hyperplanes, where b_i = 0, and of a family of spheres when no b_i vanishes, by one Q_n-reflection from the configuration of two parallel hyperplanes and n unit spheres in the proof of GLMWY III's Theorem 6.1, or from its inversion in the unit sphere. Congruence: two valid, pairwise tangent families with the same curvatures, index by index, are carried one to the other by exactly one Euclidean motion x -> x O + t with O^T O = I, reflections and hyperplanes included, with O = (1/2) X^T Q_n X' and t = -(1/4) a^T Q_n X' for augmented matrices [a | b | X] and [a' | b | X'] and the motion's action on points, spheres and hyperplanes; W_1^-1 W_2 preserves the target form and fixes the curvature coordinate, and every such matrix is a motion matrix (GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 argue instead by the rigidity of a simplex of centres); its uniqueness and parameters are proved here. A motion preserves validity, curvature and tangency, so two valid, pairwise tangent families are congruent exactly when their curvature vectors agree. For every solution W: the total curvature B is nonzero, the open sets {y : B F_i(y) < 0}, F_i(y) = b_i |y|^2 - 2 <v_i, y> + a_i the power polynomial of row i (negative exactly inside a ball, outside a ball of negative radius, or on the side of a hyperplane its normal points to), are pairwise disjoint, at most two rows are hyperplanes, and no three boundaries pass through a finite point; for a valid, pairwise tangent family the total curvature is nonzero, at most two members are hyperplanes, and when the total curvature is positive the open interiors are pairwise disjoint. The converse of Theorem 3.2 in every dimension under the hypothesis of a nonzero first column (every real M with M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) and a nonzero first column is the curvature-centre matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes), which GLMWY I, Theorem 3.1 and its Remark, prove at n = 2 with that hypothesis and which LMW's printed converse ("any real solution M") and GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 Theorem 2.3 omit, together with the matrix at n = 2 with columns 0, e_0 - e_1, e_2 - e_3 (GLMWY I's configuration (3.15) with its first column zeroed; the matrix of four oriented lines with normals +-e_0, +-e_1), which solves the equation and is the curvature-centre matrix of no valid, pairwise tangent family. The existence of a configuration in every dimension (that configuration); for n >= 2 the Apollonian generators S_k = I + (2/(n-1)) e_k 1^T - (2n/(n-1)) e_k e_k^T of GLMWY III, (4.1), preserve Q_n and carry configurations to configurations, with the row formula (S_k W)_k = (2/(n-1)) sum_{i != k} W_i - W_k, and Soddy's two spheres (LMW, footnote 3; GLMWY III, Section 4.1), in the signed sense: the oriented spheres and hyperplanes tangent to n + 1 members of a configuration are exactly the missing member and its Apollonian reflection, two distinct objects whose curvatures sum to (2/(n-1)) times the sum of the others' curvatures. The planar Soddy-Gosset relation for four circles of positive radius, pairwise externally tangent or with one enclosing circle, is already in Lean in facebookresearch/atlas-lean (descartes_circle_theorem, not registered); rjwalters/lean-genius and carlok/LeanFrontier treat the planar relation as a definition (its two roots, the same over the complex numbers, integer reflections and parity; LeanFrontier checks it for one family of Ford circles and their tangent line), with no derivation from tangency; no other formalization of these statements was found by the dated searches.

candidates.title: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

candidates.title: BrandonMYates/schwarzschild-comparator
candidates.abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.

candidates.abstract:
A conditional Lean 4 formalization of E. Markman, "Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds" (arXiv:2502.03415v2). The paper proves that the Hodge-Weil classes of polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 are algebraic (Theorem 1.5.1) and deduces the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.6.1).

Every result of the paper about cohomology classes, Clifford algebras, spin representations, Hodge structures and period domains is proved in a linear-algebra model of the cohomology of abelian varieties (abelian varieties up to isogeny as polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight one), by the paper's arguments except the departures listed under fidelity (notably Proposition 6.1.2 and Lemma 4.0.2, proved by other arguments with the owner's approval): rational secant lines to the spinor variety and the abelian 2n-folds of Weil type they give (Sections 2-4), the Spin(V)-equivariance of Orlov's equivalence (Section 6, Proposition 6.1.2), Theorem 1.4.1(3) and (4) (the characteristic class of the secant-square sheaf stays of Hodge type on every Weil-type deformation of X x X^, and its K-translates with h^3 span Q h^3 + HW), Corollary 1.3.2, the cohomological results of Section 8, and Section 10. The results the paper cites from Chevalley, Igusa (Lemmas 1-2, Section 2, Proposition 3 except the orbits over subfields in which -d is not a square), Golyshev-Lunts-Orlov, Orlov, Huybrechts, Trautman, van Geemen (Def. 4.9, and Th. 5.2(3) through Landherr's theorem and Meyer's theorem), Markman (2023) and Schoen (Prop. 10, from push-forward of cycles, by Voisin's argument) are proved in the case the paper uses.

Theorem 1.5.1 and Corollary 1.6.1 are proved assuming, as named hypotheses in their statements, the paper's own sheaf-theoretic Sections 7-9 (in the form: the class kappa_3(E) is algebraic near X x X^ wherever kappa(E) is of Hodge type) and results from algebraic geometry not yet available in Lean: about algebraic cycles, pullbacks, push-forwards along projections and products of algebraic classes, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Voisin's algebraicity loci and a theorem of Ramon-Mari; about Hodge structures, two theorems of Moonen-Zarhin. Remark 10.1.2(1) assumes part of Igusa's Proposition 3 when -d is not a square. Eleven statements of the paper are false or misprinted as printed and are formalized in corrected form (the basis of Example 10.2.2 is also misprinted, with no effect on the value computed there); REPORT.md audits the paper.

routes.title: A compact subset that cannot escape to infinity by homotopy

candidates.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
candidates.abstract:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.

candidates.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
candidates.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.

candidates.title: Curvature-Induced Killing at Stochastic Algebraic Folds
candidates.abstract: We study the lifetime of a regular algebraic branch under continuous forcing and infinite-activity tangent jumps. For a parabolic fold, a first-order tangent kick decreases the discriminant by an exact quadratic amount. Symmetric stable marks of index $\alpha\in(0,2)$ therefore generate a one-sided normal jump kernel of index $q=\alpha/2$, with a coefficient determined by curvature. The normal diffusion and jump amplitudes depend on the evolving tangential state. We compute the full killed generator on powers of the discriminant and obtain occupation and terminal-jump bounds for this same joint process. Uniformly subcritical normal drift gives finite censored boundary lifetime and finite cumulative killing rate; continuous contact and jump exit both have positive probability. At and above the uniform critical threshold, a logarithmic nonlocal barrier excludes censored boundary contact, and the original branch terminates at a jump almost surely. A comparison after a stochastic time change yields an explicit stretched-exponential upper bound for survival and hence all positive lifetime moments. In the subcritical regime, an optimized upper bound for the probability of jump termination tends to zero as the curvature coefficient or the initial discriminant tends to zero. The analysis combines power estimates for the jump generator with a logarithmic barrier at the critical threshold. Numerical calculations illustrate the dependence of terminal causes on curvature.

candidates.title: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation
candidates.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

candidates.title: Almost all Markoff numbers are unique.
candidates.abstract:
A Markoff number is the largest coordinate of a positive integer solution of
$a^2+b^2+c^2=3abc$. Frobenius conjectured in 1913 that every Markoff number
is the largest coordinate of exactly one such solution with $a\le b\le c$.
We prove that the conjecture holds for almost all Markoff numbers: the
proportion of exceptions among the Markoff numbers up to $X$ tends to $0$
as $X\to\infty$.

Two such solutions with the same largest coordinate give simple closed
geodesics of equal length on the modular torus, that is, primitive homology
classes $v,w$ with equal values $N(v)=N(w)$ of the McShane--Rivin stable
norm $N$. Estimates for the boundary of the unit ball of $N$ reduce the
problem to the equations $N(Gv)=N(v)$ with $G$ a rational linear map. For
each $G$ that is not a symmetry of the torus, a zero-one law for the
$3$-adic analytic dynamics of the mapping class group on the Markoff
surface shows that the solutions $v$ have density zero.
